Even as I talked at length, Yoo Joonghyuk gave no reply.
Something felt strange, so I looked up. Yoo Joonghyuk was looking down at me with a serious gaze.
“Kim Dokja, what is your objective?”
“Objective? What objective?”
“Is reaching ‘the end of all scenarios’ your ultimate goal?”
I hesitated briefly before answering.
“Well, more or less.”
“Can you promise that, no matter what happens, you will not give up on that goal?”
······What was with this bastard all of a sudden?
I wanted to laugh it off, but seeing Yoo Joonghyuk ask without any change in his expression, I couldn't help becoming serious too.
“Of course I won't give up. But why?”
“It's nothing.”
Yoo Joonghyuk withdrew his gaze from me and looked toward the others. His left eyebrow was twitching. Watching that eyebrow wriggle like a caterpillar left an uneasy chill in one corner of my heart.
Having read Ways of Survival to the end, I know.
Yoo Joonghyuk's left eyebrow only twitches when he has made a grave decision.
And after he makes a grave decision, there is always a high likelihood of death followed by regression.
Wondering what nonsense this bastard was plotting now, I was just about to use [Omniscient Reader's Viewpoint] when the others arrived. Before I could even open my mouth, Yoo Joonghyuk beat me to it.
“I will announce the participants in the tenth scenario.”
The backlash against Yoo Joonghyuk's unilateral announcement was enormous.
“How can he just decide that all by himself?”
Once Yoo Joonghyuk had finished his arbitrary announcement and disappeared, Jung Heewon was the first to shout.
“‘We leave in three days! Raise your rankings by then yourselves!’ He says that and walks off, and we're supposed to scramble around on our own?”
“Why didn't you say that while that bastard was here?”
“······Would you have, Dokja-ssi?”
“No.”
Jung Heewon was still fuming, apparently unable to get over her anger.
“Still, doing what Yoo Joonghyuk says will probably give us a better chance of survival.”
“Whose side are you on, Dokja-ssi?”
I glanced at Yoo Joonghyuk, who was glaring our way from a distance, then shrugged and smiled.
“First of all, it's good to see everyone. This makes my third resurrection.”

Only then did the companions who had been frozen by Yoo Joonghyuk's overbearing presence begin to smile awkwardly, one by one. Lee Gilyoung and Shin Yoosung each clung tightly to one of my legs, while Lee Hyunsung nodded with a slightly melancholy expression.
“Congratulations on your resurrection. It's happened several times already, but I still can't get used to it.”
“I think I'd be sad if you did get used to it. For now, let's sort things out.”
Yoo Joonghyuk's unilateral announcement had been as follows.
—We will divide into two teams. My team and Kim Dokja's team. Each will be allotted four people.
—The four joining my team will be Lee Hyunsung, Gong Pildu, Lee Jihye, and Lee Seolhwa.
—Kim Dokja's team will consist of these four: Jung Heewon, Shin Yoosung, Lee Gilyoung, and Yoo Sangah.

In the end, the roster was more or less the same as the core group that had taken part in our battles so far. He meant for the companions who had been fighting together all along to take on the tenth scenario too. Perhaps he was being considerate of me, or perhaps it was convenient for him. Given Yoo Joonghyuk's personality, the latter was probably far more likely.
No one seemed particularly dissatisfied with the roster itself. The only person looking downcast was Lee Hyunsung.
“I'd like to be on your team, Dokja-ssi······.”
“We're all going together anyway, so it probably won't matter much which team you're on.”
I patted Lee Hyunsung's shoulder and turned toward the others.
The first person whose eyes met mine was Yoo Sangah.
Perhaps it had been too long, because even meeting her eyes somehow felt strange. After a moment, Jung Heewon poked me in the side.
“What is it? Can't get the garter belt and qipao out of your head?”
“······Are we still talking about that?”
“It was that shocking. We even gave it a name among ourselves: ‘The Kim Dokja Garter Belt Incident.’ But I'd rather die than wear one.”
“I wasn't hoping you would.”
At that, Lee Jihye shot her hand up.
“I'd be willing to wear one if it performed well! SSS-grade!”
“Stop teasing me.”
“I could wear something like that too, as long as its performance was good.”
“Why you too, Hyunsung-ssi······?”
“A soldier isn't picky about equipment.”
I was about to advise him not to exercise his soldierly spirit in such an odd direction when Uriel's message sounded from empty space.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ says that the constellation who made the garter belt was also a man.]
That had to be a joke, right? Damn it.
And a ‘constellation,’ at that?
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ smiles and says she will invite him over sometime.]
Come to think of it, this whole situation was Persephone's fault. If I ever went to the Underworld again, I'd definitely have to take it up with her.
“Let's leave that subject there······ What are everyone's rankings? You all know you have to be in the top ten to be on this roster, right?”
My companions answered in turn.
Jung Heewon went first.
“I'm fourth. Grandma Lee Boksoon passed her ranking on to me.”
“I'm eighth and Shin Yoosung is ninth, hyung. Oh, and I'm higher than Shin Yoosung!”
“I'm fifth. And Gong Pildu-ssi has stepped away for a while to raise his ranking. Han Sooyoung-ssi too.”
Right, there was Han Sooyoung.
As though she had read my thoughts, Yoo Sangah asked.
“Han Sooyoung-ssi wasn't on that roster. Are you leaving her behind?”
“No, we need to bring her. Han Sooyoung is quite helpful.”
Yoo Sangah smiled weakly at the mention of Han Sooyoung.
The others still didn't know that she had been the ‘First Apostle.’
Whenever Han Sooyoung came up, Yoo Sangah would feel as though she was lying, so she couldn't help feeling bad. I'd have to tell them about it sometime, but I wasn't sure I'd get the chance.
Jung Heewon, who had been listening beside us, spoke.
“Only ten people can go up in total. How are you going to bring Han Sooyoung-ssi?”

“In principle, only ten can go, but there's a hidden piece. One of the items you can obtain in the [Dark Castle] is called a [Six Man Card]. If you use it, someone who isn't on a team can participate in the next scenario too.”

“······Honestly, those damned hidden pieces. Is there anything else you could tell us? We ought to know what's coming in the next scenario that warrants all this fuss. You're always whispering with Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi, just the two of you.”
“Whispering? I'm not very comfortable with that wording.”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ snorts through her nose.]
Jung Heewon looked at me with a bright smile.
“Then tell us. Show us you're different from Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi, Kim Dokja-ssi.”
When I looked around, everyone was gazing at me with shining eyes, like grandchildren waiting for their grandmother to tell them a folktale.
If I were a storyteller, I might have opened with something fitting like ‘Once upon a time, there lived a hero.’ But I'm Kim Dokja, a reader, not Kim Jakga, a writer.
“Have any of you heard of beings called ‘Demon Kings’?”
Demon King (魔王).
At the unexpected term, my companions looked at one another.
“Well······ A king of demons? Something like that?”
“I know! They're in anime all the time!”
I nodded at Lee Gilyoung's shout.
“More or less.”
It was a little different according to the lore of Ways of Survival, but this wasn't the place to ramble through an explanation.
“The tenth scenario is a scenario where we fight that ‘Demon King.’”
Lee Hyunsung nodded with a low hum.
“Dokkaebis, returnees, tentacle monsters······ I did think it was about time something like a Demon King appeared.”
Lee Jihye, who had been listening, asked.
“But isn't a Demon King ridiculously strong? That demon marquis was already that powerful······ Just how strong is it compared to that?”
I considered for a moment before answering.
“Constellation-level.”
There was a phrase used to describe Demon Kings in Ways of Survival.
Constellations (星座) who had not ascended.
Quite literally, Demon Kings were ‘constellations’ who had remained rooted in the mortal world.
Her face turning pale, Lee Jihye pressed me.
“How are we supposed to beat something like that? Oh, are you and Master going to beat it yourselves again, ajusshi?”
“No, this time we'll all beat it together.”
“······Can't I just not go up?”
“We can only beat it if we all fight together. It was pure luck that Yoo Joonghyuk and I defeated that god. We won't get a lucky break like that twice.”
“Don't worry. It's true that Demon Kings are as strong as ‘constellations,’ but the one upstairs isn't quite at that level.”
“Then?”
I hesitated briefly.
I wasn't sure I could spill that much information all at once right now.
Because this information concerned not only Demon Kings, but also the constellations of the <Star Stream>.
After thinking for a moment, I was just about to explain through [Group Chat] when—
[I'll explain that.]
Perhaps aware of my predicament, a voice came from empty space.
[It's been a while, everyone. Ah, you have no idea how frustrating it's been, not being able to speak······ Haha, are your scenario preparations going well?]
It was Bihyung.
Originally, only 72 beings were recognized as ‘Demon Kings’ in the <Star Stream>.
Like constellations, they had modifiers, and each controlled a different domain in the Demon Realm.
Though they couldn't compare to a ‘nebula,’ they were still beings who led a ‘faction.’
They mocked the constellations' obsession with their honor as constellations and remained on land that even the dokkaebis had abandoned.
Perhaps that was why. The constellations had come to hate Demon Kings as much as ‘Outer Gods,’ and this [Dark Castle] scenario had been created with that inclination in mind.
Watch incarnations fight, and kill a Demon King too.
You could say it was a scenario made to give the constellations a satisfying payoff.
“Oh, please! I told you I'm not going!”
Drag, drag, drag, drag.
Over those three days, I tracked down Han Sooyoung, who had been hiding on the outskirts of the [Dark Castle].

She had hidden herself so thoroughly that I might never have found her without the [Binding Rope] and [Person Search] I'd purchased from the Dokkaebi Bag. Han Sooyoung shouted as she struggled desperately.
“I'm not fighting anymore! I'm just going to sit around here, then leave once you clear the scenario!”
“You have to come too.”
“I don't want to fight a Demon King!”
“The 73rd Demon King was thrown together for this. You know that too, don't you?”

As I'd said earlier, only 72 beings in the <Star Stream> had been recognized as having the Status of a ‘Demon King.’ Yet this scenario was titled [The 73rd Demon King]. In other words, the one upstairs wasn't an ‘official Demon King.’
“It's still a ‘Demon King,’ so it'll be one of the strongest beings we've encountered so far. But it isn't as strong as a Narrative-grade constellation. We have a fighting chance.”
“The difficulty might have changed. How many times has it changed while I've been with you?”
“Dokkaebis can't arbitrarily change a main scenario's difficulty. That's under the <Star Stream>'s jurisdiction.”
“You think dokkaebis are the only danger? Have you already forgotten what happened three days ago?”
It wasn't strange that Han Sooyoung was so thoroughly fed up.
Knowing the original story's course would only make it worse.
“If we keep going through the scenarios like this, all your companions will be wiped out before long. You know the <nebulas> are all after you right now, don't you?”
“······I know. That's why I'm preparing carefully too.”
“Preparing? Seriously, is this something preparation can fix? How do you know what'll happen even in the very next scenario?”
We had just reached the campsite, so I silently pointed toward the others.
My companions were training in their respective formations. Facing an imagined enemy, they shifted formation and practiced combining their skills.
“Gilyoung and Yoosung, to the rear! Yoo Sangah-ssi moves forward, and I'll take the position behind her!”
“Got it!”

Their calm, coordinated attacks were on an entirely different level from anything they'd done before. They used elemental properties to stack damage, and took advantage of the enemy's attack radius to rain down fire from a distance. Watching them closely, Han Sooyoung's mouth fell open.
“Wait, is that······ Did you analyze the Demon King's attack patterns?”
I nodded.
“Yes.”
“How much?”
“Almost all of them.”
It wasn't impossible.

I had the text file of Ways of Survival, and a considerable database of Yoo Joonghyuk's battles with the 73rd Demon King had accumulated. Moreover, Yoo Joonghyuk had fought the 73rd Demon King in his second round too. With practical experience and thorough theoretical knowledge combined, developing a complete strategy for the next scenario wasn't entirely impossible.
Han Sooyoung looked genuinely overwhelmed.
“······You really are a crazy bastard.”
“Do you still think the next scenario will be difficult?”
The 73rd Demon King was strong, but if we went up with preparations this thorough, there would be no problem.
It might even turn out to be the easiest scenario we'd attempted so far.
Before long, the companions who had been training gathered around us one by one.
“Has everyone finished raising their rankings?”
Jung Heewon answered on everyone's behalf.
“We're all in the top ten. Jihye and Pildu-ssi were actually cutting it close, but they moved up automatically this morning.”
“Automatically?”
That kind of advancement occurred in only one circumstance.
When a higher-ranked person died.
Han Sooyoung already looked apprehensive.
“A top-ten ranker suddenly died? Something's strange······ Hey, I really think I'd be better off not going······.
“You're here, Kim Dokja. Are you bringing that woman too?”
At Yoo Joonghyuk's sudden appearance, Han Sooyoung swiftly hid behind me.
Apparently she was still afraid of Yoo Joonghyuk.
When I nodded, Yoo Joonghyuk, who had been glaring disapprovingly at Han Sooyoung, took a [Six Man Card] out of his clothes.
[Incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ has used a Six Man Card.]
[Incarnation ‘Han Sooyoung’ is recruited as a special participant in the scenario.]
[Incarnation ‘Han Sooyoung’ has joined the team of incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’.]
Han Sooyoung was horrified by the messages that appeared.
“Wh-what is this! Hey! Why am I on his team!”
“All right, we're about to leave, so everyone get ready.”
At my words, everyone gathered by team.
Yoo Joonghyuk's team assembled first.
In order: Lee Seolhwa, Lee Jihye, Lee Hyunsung, and Gong Pildu. Plus Han Sooyoung, still complaining.
The sight of elements from the original story strangely mingled with things outside it stirred an odd feeling in me.
A luxury only the reader of Ways of Survival could enjoy, perhaps.
My team then lined up in turn.
Jung Heewon, Yoo Sangah, Shin Yoosung. And Lee Gilyoung too.
Compared with Yoo Joonghyuk's disciplined team, ours had a relaxed atmosphere.
I looked at each of my companions with care.
“······What's with that sappy look?”
“Nothing. It just feels different, looking back······.”
Despite Jung Heewon's reproach, I quietly smiled.
Looking at these people who had followed me faithfully all this way, my heart somehow swelled, yet for some reason it ached too.
That feeling seemed especially strong since I'd spoken with the [Fourth Wall].
Perhaps that was why I had prepared even more thoroughly for this scenario.
I was now afraid of losing them.
“Oh, you know our team has a sixth member too, right?”
At my words, my teammates turned their heads, following my gaze.
A figure stood hesitantly a few steps away.
“Don't stay over there. Come here.”
We had obtained a total of two [Six Man Cards].
Just as Han Sooyoung had joined Yoo Joonghyuk's team, our team had a sixth man too.
A sixth woman, to be precise.
“······Sookyung-ssi wanted to go with you too.”
“Right now, it will be more helpful to have you with us.”
Jeon Woochi's incarnation, Cho Youngran, looked at me with mixed emotions in her eyes.
I had asked my mother to let me include her in this expedition as a special addition.
Because quite a few of Jeon Woochi's stigmas could prove useful in an emergency.
“Have you talked with Sookyung-ssi?”
“A little.”
Perhaps because of the aftereffects of emerging from the [Fourth Wall], my mother was in no condition to participate in the next scenario.
Through the [Fourth Wall], I had learned many things about my mother.
Not only about the past she'd hidden, but also about what she'd experienced after joining the scenarios.
Unlike me, who knew every story in the original novel, my mother had endured one desperate struggle after another.

She had repeatedly paid exorbitant prices to obtain help from constellations, deliberately let the reincarnator Nirvana capture her to steal their memories, and even entered a contract with a <nebula> to protect me.
Yet even after learning all of that, I couldn't find anything to say to my mother.
I decided to think that perhaps the time simply hadn't come yet.
Someday, once the scenarios had ended safely, the day would come when we, mother and son, could share a real ‘story.’
Perhaps my mother knew that too, because she didn't say much this time. She merely looked at me for a long time, then turned her eyes away and said this.
—I trust your choice.
I didn't know why, but hearing those words gave me a strange feeling.
Perhaps, just as I had read my mother through the [Fourth Wall], she too had read something in me.
“Let's go.”
We began to move.
Our destination was the altar at the center of the <Abyss Plains>.
As on the first floor of the Dark Castle, we could use an altar here to move to the next floor.
Perhaps bored by the walk, Jung Heewon spoke.
“It bothers me that the nebulas are so quiet.”
In fact, we hadn't heard any messages from the nebulas for two days.
I still couldn't tell whether they were concealing some scheme or whether it was because they'd consumed too much probability. Looking toward Yoo Sangah, I asked.
“Are you able to contact <Olympus>?”
“······I haven't been able to for three days.”
The last I'd heard, the constellations of <Olympus> were currently divided.

The ones who had approached Yoo Sangah so far were the outsiders of <Olympus>, including Dionysus and Persephone. Perhaps the incident three days ago had led to an internal power struggle within <Olympus> too.
Perhaps my expression looked uneasy, because Yoo Sangah spoke with concern in her voice.
“Dokja-ssi, are you all right?”
“I'm fine. And you, Yoo Sangah-ssi?”
“······I'm trying to be.”
I looked at Yoo Sangah.
Someone so kind that the longer I looked at her, the more I somehow ended up feeling guilty.
I'd already heard plenty about how she'd been the first to learn of my [Fate] and had run all over the place trying to save me.
That wasn't unusual for Yoo Sangah.
She was always the first to step forward when something was wrong.
She had also been the first to stand up to save the old woman in the first scenario. So even if someone else had been in my place now, Yoo Sangah would have acted just as she had.
“We can overcome this, can't we? We always have so far, so this time too······.”
“Don't worry.”
I spoke as if to reassure Yoo Sangah.
“I won't die. You know that.”
Since Yoo Sangah had been the first to see my Fate, she would also know it hadn't disappeared.
As I briefly considered what else I could say to reassure her, Yoo Joonghyuk's voice came from ahead.
“We're here.”
An enormous structure reminiscent of the ancient Parthenon stood before us.
Seeing my companions visibly stiffen, I spoke to them one by one.
“Gilyoung. Yoosung. Just do what we practiced earlier. Don't summon the Chimera Dragon until I give the signal, no matter what. Understood?”
The children's role was the most important in the battle against the Demon King. The Chimera Dragon they had tamed would play a crucial part in this fight.

“Yoo Sangah-ssi, please protect Jung Heewon-ssi from injury as much as possible. And Jung Heewon-ssi, you'll be our main damage dealer again. You've thoroughly familiarized yourself with the strategy, right?”
“I remember it.”

When Yoo Joonghyuk finished his preparations and looked our way, I brought my companions closer too. Soon, a waist-high altar came into view. Yoo Joonghyuk and I placed our hands on the palm marks atop the altar at the same time.
[Scenario challengers confirmed.]
[Scenario Challenger: Yoo Joonghyuk, Dark Castle Rank 1]
[Scenario Challenger: Kim Dokja, Dark Castle Rank 2]
[Total Entrants: 12]
[Would you like to enter the scenario?]
We nodded simultaneously.
Whooooooosh!
With a dazzling beam of light, our bodies began to be transported to the next floor.
We arrived in a narrow passage.
[You have entered a new main scenario area.]
[Main Scenario # 10 — ‘The 73rd Demon King’ begins!]
As expected, events were unfolding exactly as in the original story.
If we followed this passage all the way, we would probably reach the hall where the 73rd Demon King resided.
“Everyone, get into formation.”

Keeping low, we moved cautiously along the passage. The difficulty of the battle against the Demon King depended on how much damage we could inflict with the opening ambush. If we could approach as quietly as possible and deal substantial damage, we might finish the battle smoothly without even using all the formations we'd practiced.
But as we moved along the passage, an uneasy feeling crossed my mind.
······Why was it so quiet?
Shouldn't we be able to sense the Demon King's presence by now?
That was when a system message appeared.
[An error has occurred in the scenario.]
“Hyung, what's this······?”
When a startled Lee Gilyoung instinctively spoke, I brought a finger to my lips. The others began murmuring in even lower voices.
“Dokja-ssi, this is somehow different from what you told us······.”
“Th-there are dead people here······!”
It was Lee Hyunsung, who had been finding the way at the front, who said it.
Moving as stealthily as possible, we gathered around Lee Hyunsung.
To our surprise, there were corpses there that didn't appear to have been dead for long.
The moment Yoo Joonghyuk touched a corpse, powerful sparks flew up.
“Traces of a probability storm.”

I didn't know what they had done, but if sparks remained even after death, their sponsors must have overextended themselves considerably too. They seemed to have drawn on immense power through Incarnation Synchronization. With traces this severe, their sponsors would also have suffered damage close to annihilation.
The question was who had done this, and why.
Yoo Joonghyuk spoke.
“They are the terminal incarnations of <Vedas> and <Papyrus>.”
“What?”
“I encountered them while traveling through the [Dark Castle]. They're definitely the ones who approached me.”
“······How did they get here? If they were terminals for the nebulas, their rankings would have been high enough, but they shouldn't have had the right to participate in the scenario.”
“It seems there were more [Six Man Cards].”
That resolved one unanswered question. Lee Jihye and Gong Pildu's rankings had suddenly risen because these people had died here.
My foreboding grows worse.
What if the nebulas had been quiet because they'd poured their remaining probability into this place?
Then that meant······?
Yoo Joonghyuk and I instinctively looked at each other, then forgot our formations and began sprinting toward the hall.
If I was right, this was no time to worry about formations.
And the moment we reached the hall, we witnessed a shocking sight.
[Honestly, constellation-nims. What on earth have you been doing?]
Dozens of dokkaebis floated in the air at the center of the enormous hall.
[You put us in a difficult position when you do things like this at your own discretion. Aren't you taking the <Star Stream> too lightly? Using <Deus Ex Machina> in a place like this?]
The words weren't directed at us, but they clearly seemed intended for us to hear. I saw Bihyung awkwardly turn his head away when our eyes met.
These bastards, what the hell······.

[I understand that you cherish your incarnations, but interfering with probability won't end the scenario. A few of you seem to have suffered damage close to annihilation. Why on earth did you do this?]
A strange smile rested on the lips of the dokkaebi speaking on their behalf.
A smile that made it seem as though the dokkaebi had known from the start that this would happen.
But wait.
What had that bastard just said?
“Kim Dokja.”
At Yoo Joonghyuk's words, I looked where he was pointing.
The center of the hall.
The throne where the ‘73rd Demon King’ should have been was shattered.
And the Demon King who should have greeted us with a menacing presence—
[The ‘73rd Demon King’ is currently dead.]
was dead, its chest brutally torn open.
“Wh-what is this? Is it dead?”
At the words of Han Sooyoung, who had arrived a little later, the others also spoke.
“The Demon King's already dead?”
“Then what happens to the scenario?”
“······Could it already be over?”
My mind was so tangled that I could barely hear my companions' voices.
Incarnations who hadn't even qualified to challenge the scenario had killed the Demon King with the nebulas' support, accepting the cost of a probability storm.
At first glance, it looked as though the scenario had been resolved.
But the main scenarios of the <Star Stream> weren't that simple.
[The <Star Stream> restores the scenario's balance.]
A scenario ruined by excessive intervention from transcendent beings was forcibly restored through the probability of the <Star Stream>.
A powerful sense of déjà vu flashed through my mind.

It hadn't been the scenario [The 73rd Demon King], but something similar had happened in Ways of Survival. A scenario had been ruined by the constellations' rampage, and the <Star Stream> had restored the main scenario.
What exactly had happened then?
[The <Star Stream> corrects the damaged probability.]
I looked at the spot where the Demon King had died.

The <Star Stream> preferred stories to flow naturally, so it wouldn't bring a dead being back to life just because something like this had happened. Reversing time or resurrecting someone without foreshadowing did the greatest damage to a scenario's probability.
[The main scenario's contents have been updated!]
The 73rd Demon King was dead.
But a 73rd Demon King was still needed.
Because the scenario could only progress if we hunted it down.
What the <Star Stream> would do to resolve this contradiction had been decided from the outset.
A precious orb (寶玉) gleaming black lay where the Demon King had died.
I instinctively spoke.
“Hey, that······.”
But I can't sense the presence that should be right beside me.
A chilling sensation spread down my spine.
Time seemed to pass very slowly.
When I turned, Yoo Joonghyuk was already gone from my side.
“Yoo Joonghyuk!”
By the time I moved, Yoo Joonghyuk had already reached the orb.
The expression on his face as he looked back at me was one I'd never seen before.
Yoo Joonghyuk was looking at me with a gaze that had never appeared anywhere in Ways of Survival.
“Kim Dokja. Make sure you keep your promise.”
Then a system message sounded.
[The orb has selected a ‘Candidate for the 73rd Demon King.’]
[A new ‘73rd Demon King’ is selected.]
“Hey! What the fuck are you talking about!”
Shouting urgently, I ran toward Yoo Joonghyuk.
A pitch-black aura began surging from Yoo Joonghyuk's body as he held the orb.
[The being chosen by the orb evolves into a Demon King!]
The one chosen by the orb becomes the 73rd Demon King.
—······Can you promise that, no matter what happens, you will not give up on that goal?
Yoo Joonghyuk's meaningful question from a few days earlier crossed my mind.
My goal. Reaching the end of all these scenarios······.
Could he······? No, there was no way.
I shouted almost convulsively.
“Yoo Joonghyuk, you bastard!”
That was when I heard steel wires slicing through the air with a shiiiing.
Dozens of wires extended from behind me and swept toward Yoo Joonghyuk. One of them snatched the orb from his hand.
[Demon King succession is canceled.]
Yoo Joonghyuk's face filled with bewilderment.
“Dokja-ssi!”

When I turned, Yoo Sangah was extending dozens of threads from her hands. While everyone else had frozen, she alone had collected herself and acted resourcefully. Ensnared in [Thread Binding], the Demon King's orb was flying toward us along the threads. Yoo Joonghyuk released an immense burst of murderous intent and roared.
“Do not interfere!”
Just as a powerful wave of magic was about to strike Yoo Sangah, I activated [Way of the Wind] through [Bookmark] and deflected it.
Kwakakakakakoom!
Even with [Way of the Wind] at its maximum level, deflecting it wasn't easy. This was the power of Yoo Joonghyuk, now a transcendent. Gritting my teeth, I shouted.
“Yoo Sangah-ssi! Hold on to that! Don't use it under any circumstances!”
“Yes!”
The others were scrambling about, unable to understand what on earth was happening.
Han Sooyoung split off dozens of avatars and shouted.
“I knew this would happen! Kim Dokja, I told you! Yoo Joonghyuk is a bastard who only ever thinks of himself!”
Apparently misunderstanding the situation, Han Sooyoung screamed at the top of her lungs.
“Kim Dokja! You have to stop him! That fucker's obviously planning to become the Demon King, kill everyone, and clear the scenario by himself······!”
Bangbangbangbangboom!
Han Sooyoung's avatars blocking Yoo Joonghyuk exploded all at once, and her main body was slammed into the hall's wall.

Grumbling, Laziness, Sloth, Lethargy······.

Who would look at this kid’s character information and think this was the second protagonist of ‘Ways of Survival’? If Yoo Joonghyuk had seen it, his pride would have been wounded to learn that someone like this was on the same list of protagonists.
“Y-you, how did you······!”
But Jang Hayoung hadn’t always been like this.
Because Jang Hayoung had tried, and tried again, but things hadn’t worked out.
Because a massive ‘wall’ had always stood in the way.
It was simply what happened when the results failed to match the effort.
“Oh, right. You don’t use your real name here. Should I call you ‘Aslan,’ then?”
“How do you know my real name!”
Startled, Jang Hayoung pressed flat against the wall.
Watching that, I recalled an old memory.
―Author-nim. I was thinking, maybe this would be a good time to create a new character······.
If I hadn’t left that comment back then······.
Would ‘Jang Hayoung’ never have existed in this world?
―And preferably a pretty female character······.
Perhaps that was why I felt responsible for this kid.
I didn’t know whether the author had created this character because of me.
―As for the backstory, hmm. Since Joonghyuk is a regressor, maybe this one could be a dimensional mover······.
At least, if I hadn’t posted that comment back then, this ‘second protagonist’ could at least have been spared being dragged into another dimension.
“You don’t lack talent. You just don’t know what your talent is.”
“What? Wh-what are you talking about······!”
Just as I was about to speak again, the door burst open.
“What is it, Aslan? What’s all this noise?”
“A-Aileen!”
After taking a look at Jang Hayoung’s face, Aileen turned to me.
“What’s your deal? What did you do to the kid?”
I shrugged without a word.
I could see several people behind Aileen.
They were probably the [Syswitz Civil Council].
The last voices of conscience here in [Syswitz], standing against the duke’s ambitions.
I liked people like that.
Jang Hayoung could wait. Should I deal with these people first?
“Duke Syswitz······.”
“What?”
“He’s an ambitious fellow. He turned down a high-ranking position in another great Demon Realm to come all the way out to this frontier.”
At my words, the council members exchanged glances.
As I spoke, I looked straight at Aileen in particular.
“Duke Syswitz probably asked you to build him a Giant Soldier. Didn’t he?”
“Huh?”
“He went a little off the rails after touring the Underworld recently. That’s why he’s making such an unreasonable request of you. He doesn’t know his own limits.”
“H-how on earth do you······!”
As I reeled off information they hadn’t even told me, the council members grew visibly flustered. I saw Aileen’s body go rigid with shock. I seized the opportunity and continued.
“But this makes your third refusal, so next time he’ll take you by force. Are you ready for that?”
At my words, the faces of Aileen and the other citizens abruptly darkened.
That was understandable.
They were formidable figures on their own planets, but they didn’t have the power to rival a duke of the Demon Realm.
After enjoying the silence for a little while, I smiled and continued.
“Agree to my conditions, and I’ll stop the ‘duke’ for you.”
They must have found this bewildering.
An exile who had suddenly appeared knew everything about them and was even making an absurd offer.
It was Aileen who finally managed to speak.
“You······ who on earth are you?”
Right. Whatever came next, this was where it would begin.
It would have been nice to say, ‘I am Kim Dokja,’ but I couldn’t do that yet.
If I revealed my name here, Earth’s constellations might learn that I was still alive.
Then······ should I follow the original this time?
Recalling the 111th round in the original novel, I continued in the most sinister voice I could muster.
“My name is Yoo Joonghyuk. I am the one who will become the ‘Demon King’ of this, the 73rd Demon Realm.”
[Your notoriety is spreading in the 73rd Demon Realm.]
At the sudden message, Yoo Joonghyuk looked up at the sky.
Of course, the sky gave no answer.
Then, for an instant, a peculiar change came over Yoo Joonghyuk’s expression.
After thinking for a moment, Yoo Joonghyuk glared at the sky with disbelief in his eyes and muttered again.
“Kim Dokja?”
Yoo Joonghyuk’s declaration about becoming the ‘73rd Demon King’ was also a line from ‘Ways of Survival.’
With a little flutter of excitement, I watched the council members’ reactions.
It was strange.
In ‘Ways of Survival,’ everyone would surely have been won over with an “Ooh!”······.
Their reactions weren’t nearly as dramatic as I’d imagined.
That was when the voice came.
「The Demon King of the 73rd Demon Realm! Aileen and the other council members were deeply shocked that anyone could so readily utter such words.」
When had this bastard woken up?
When I actually needed it, it had gone off saying it was sleepy······.
「Meanwhile, Kim Dokja somehow felt stronger.」
「It was a habit he’d had since his school days. Whenever his self-esteem faltered, or an important moment in life came along, Kim Dokja would often say those words. “I am Yoo Joonghyuk.”」
Enduring the [Fourth Wall]’s harassment as it dredged up my embarrassing past without restraint, I smacked my lips bitterly. Damn it, there was really nothing I could do about this bastard.
“Council members, please leave us for a moment. I need to speak with our guest alone.”
After some thought, Aileen made a bold decision.
Once Jang Hayoung and the council members had gone outside, Aileen pulled up a chair and sat close beside my operating table.
“How about undoing these before we talk? I’m hardly in a position to have a conversation.”
But Aileen didn’t release my restraints.
It meant she still didn’t fully trust me.
“You said you would become a Demon King.”
“Yes.”
For the moment, I nodded.
“Do you know what that means?”
“Exactly what it sounds like. Becoming the king of the 73rd Demon Realm.”
“And?”
“It also means attracting far too much attention from the other 72 Demon Kings.”
Truthfully, that part concerned me a little.
I hadn’t exactly built friendly relations with the Demon Kings yet.
Watching my expression, Aileen sighed.
“I did get a glimpse of your Story composition while treating you······ but I haven’t the slightest idea what on earth you’re thinking.”
“What’s the problem?”
“······Duke Syswitz is strong. Probably stronger than you think.”
Unlike her earlier flustered manner, Aileen’s voice was calm.
Indeed, anyone who had survived in the Demon Realm for a long time had a reason for it.
“Of course he’s strong. He is a duke, after all.”
In the Demon Realm, dukes were second in power only to Demon Kings.
Those at the pinnacle of the Demon Realm’s five noble ranks.
Some possessed power approaching that of Historical-grade constellations, so they certainly weren’t opponents to underestimate. Still, Aileen’s assessment was quite fair.
“I do understand your confidence. I’ve already confirmed that you possess remarkable Stories.”
As expected, repairing my Stories seemed to have given her some idea of my power.
She wouldn’t have had time to examine all the Stories I’d hidden, but she must have seen a couple of Legendary-grade Stories.
She had probably arranged this conversation because she’d glimpsed some potential in my Stories.
Aileen continued calmly.
“First, I need to know that you’re someone I can trust.”
“I’ll swear an Oath of Existence.”
“Nothing said here may be disclosed outside.”
With our hands pressed together, we swore an [Oath of Existence].
An oath made with one’s soul at stake.
If anyone broke this oath, they would burn up their own soul and destroy themselves. I’d once sworn this oath with Yoo Joonghyuk, too.
“I’d also like you to keep my identity to yourself.”
“I know. All the council members who participated in your Story repairs share the oath, so don’t worry.”
After a small sigh, Aileen spoke almost in a whisper, as though afraid someone might overhear.
“Our council has long been looking for an opportunity to bring down the [Factory].”
The [Factory] was the building at the heart of the [Industrial Complex], the central seat of its power.
An attempt to bring it down had an unmistakable purpose from the outset.
I knew the broad outline from reading ‘Ways of Survival,’ but I decided to ask anyway. With no way to reread ‘Ways of Survival’ right now, gathering information firsthand was important, too.
“You intend to drive out the nobles?”
“Yes.”
“But you’re all returnees, aren’t you? Why go out of your way to interfere with the Demon Realm’s ecosystem?”
“Because we aren’t returnees yet.”
In a sense, nothing could have been more accurate.
“I see.”
Not every returnee completes a dimensional travel scenario and returns home. Some returnees fail their scenarios, while others dislike their homes and remain in a foreign land. And for whatever
reason they have given up on returning, they must make that foreign land their new home. However terrible a place it may be, they have to plant their feet there and live.
“We’ve made several attempts to kill the duke.”
“Since he’s still alive, I take it they all failed.”
“······They weren’t bad plans. Not until they all failed, anyway. Among those who tried were masters from <First Murim>, and people who had become the finest swordsmen on their home planets.”
“How did you find people like that?”
“Their circumstances were similar to yours. They had all failed their homeworlds’ scenarios or been expelled from them.”
As expected, it was something I already knew.
In fact, this was precisely why Aileen treated ‘exiles.’
A means of gathering even one more powerful citizen to stand against the Ruler of the [Syswitz Industrial Complex].
That was how she used her [Story Expert] attribute.
Aileen shook her head, looking a little weary.
“Most couldn’t even get past his guards, let alone reach the duke.”
“Does he have many guards?”
“The [Factory] has a staggering hundred lower-ranking nobles of baron or viscount rank alone. There are also ten of earl rank, and two of marquis rank.”
Having so many guards was a problem.

Even lower-ranking nobles were stronger than most incarnations if they were of the demon species. Besides, all those of earl rank and above could wield the power of Stories. The bigger problem was that the duke’s power would surpass that of all his subordinates combined. But I answered as though it were no great matter.
“That’s manageable.”
“The other exiles said that, too.”
“I’m stronger than they were.”
Because that was what Yoo Joonghyuk would have said, too.
And right now, I was Yoo Joonghyuk.
But Aileen didn’t know who Yoo Joonghyuk was.
“If you were truly strong, you wouldn’t have failed your scenario.”
She was right, and for a moment I had no reply.
It would be awkward to explain now that there had been complicated circumstances.
Still, Aileen seemed to have some hope for me.
“So I’d like you to prove your ability first.”
“You mean something like this?”
As though I’d been waiting for the cue, I broke free of the restraints binding my body.
The restraints snapping with a crackle.
Aileen seemed slightly surprised, but she didn’t lose her composure.
“······The other exiles could do that much, too. I need to confirm that you can take on a noble.”
“What do you want?”
“As it happens, a suitable opponent is visiting [Syswitz].”
“You mean the envoy from the [Gilobat Industrial Complex].”
“Yes.”
I gave a little chuckle.
“I can see what you’re thinking.”
Aileen nodded.
“I’m sorry to ask this of you.”
The 73rd Demon Realm was currently in turmoil over rumors about a Demon King.
The meeting between the [Syswitz Industrial Complex] and the [Gilobat Industrial Complex] had been arranged to ease the threat of war.
“The most dangerous enemy is always your closest ally.”
If she could use that opportunity to provoke mutual slaughter (相殘), she might be able to divide the nobility within the [Syswitz Industrial Complex].
With a pawn like me now at her disposal, Aileen wouldn’t want to miss the opportunity.
Even if it failed, she had little to lose.
But I had no intention of simply letting her use me.
“Let’s make this our ‘first deal.’”
“All right. What are your conditions?”
“From now on, repair my incarnation body whenever I ask. For free, of course.”

Until my incarnation body became sturdier, I would have to keep consuming Story fragments. There was no telling when another clash between Stories might occur. For the time being, I needed Aileen’s help.
“If you succeed, I see no reason not to. Is that all?”
“One more thing.”
This was actually the main point.
“Transfer a ‘scenario’ to me.”
“······A scenario?”
This was why I’d come to the [Syswitz Industrial Complex] in the first place.
“I need your ‘Revolutionary Scenario.’”
The [Demon Realm] has long been unpopular with constellations.
Partly because constellations and Demon Kings were on bad terms, and partly because most incarnations who entered the Demon Realm were ‘failures’ to begin with.
When I left the operating room, the first thing I saw was a tavern full of citizens.
“Fuuuck, this booze tastes gooood.”
Citizens’ sighs coming from all around.
It happened to be late evening.

Workers and incarnations who had returned from a full day’s work at the [Factory] gathered in little groups, chatting and drinking. Faces screwed up as though from a bitter aftertaste. I remembered reading in ‘Ways of Survival’ that liquor in the Demon Realm was more bitter than liquor on Earth.
「Kim Dokja thought. Which of these people is the ‘Revolutionary’?」

[Scenarios] progressed even in the Demon Realm. The <Star Stream> neglected no region’s stories. In particular, the [Revolutionary Scenario], one of the main scenarios here, was watched closely even by the Demon Realm’s ‘dukes.’

―I don’t know how you learned about that scenario, but it’s difficult to help you with it right away. We don’t know who the ‘Revolutionary’ is, either. How can we even suggest transferring the scenario when we don’t know the ‘Revolutionary’s’ identity?
―You have no information at all?

―Even if we get information, the ‘Revolutionary’ changes every month, so there’s no way to know. Honestly, who would admit they’d been assigned the ‘Revolutionary’ role? There’s no telling where a ‘Spy’ might be······.
That was what Aileen had said.
But if my prediction was right, the ‘Revolutionary’ was certainly among these people.

「The [Revolutionary Scenario] was a main scenario unique to the Demon Realm. Its scenario number differed each time, but the people who encountered the scenario event were predetermined. They were the Demon Realm’s subject classes.」
At times like this, I was glad to have the [Fourth Wall].
Even without ‘Ways of Survival,’ it promptly refreshed my memory.
―The citizens here clearly remember what happened to the last person who declared themselves the ‘Revolutionary.’ So please don’t go stirring people up for nothing. You’ll make everyone anxious.
That was what Aileen had said, but I really couldn’t just wait indefinitely.
With my incarnation body somehow repaired, I could endure the [Exile Penalty] for the time being, but probably only for a few days.
「Kim Dokja thought. Only by obtaining the [Revolutionary Scenario] here can I return to my original scenario.」
Then I heard an unfamiliar voice.
“You there. Haven’t seen your face before.”
When I turned, the tavern owner was looking at me curiously.
I answered as naturally as I could.
“I only arrived yesterday.”
“Welcome, then. Life in our [Industrial Complex] is hard, but the people are good-hearted. I don’t know where you’re from, but it’s not a bad place to settle down. Care for a drink?”
“No, I’m not much of a drinker.”
“Heh heh, the Demon Realm’s hardly a place you can endure without appreciating a drink. Unfortunate fellow.”

Hearing that suddenly brought back memories of when I’d first joined ‘Mino Soft.’ At my first company dinner, Department Manager Han Myungoh had said something similar when I told him I couldn’t drink.
Come to think of it, what had become of Han Myungoh by now? After Demon King Asmodeus cursed him, I’d had no way to find out whether he was alive or dead······.
Perhaps remembering those exhausting days had something to do with it, but I was feeling a little hungry.
“I don’t drink, but I like the food that goes with it. Can I order just the food?”
“Of course. Fried claws of the Demon of Death, stir-fried demon tripe from the Lodge of Ruin, and······.”
I smiled wryly.
“You’d better stop teasing me just because I’m new here.”
“Haha, you caught me.”
“Give me whatever you make best. How much?”
“Just 5 coins.”
It was an incredibly low price.
Even a little constellation from [Peace Land] could afford to eat at that price.
After thinking for a moment, I asked.
“If I pay twice as much, can you make it twice as delicious?”
“Haha, I could even manage three times.”
When I silently handed over 50 coins, the owner’s eyes widened.
“······Ten times might be a little difficult, but I’ll give it a try.”

Despite his words, the appetizing smell suggested that the owner was quite a capable cook. I felt a little anticipation at the thought of finally satisfying my hunger. I couldn’t even remember the last time I’d eaten a proper meal.
I tried to soothe my empty stomach for the moment and let out a soft sigh.
I’d been running so hard all this time. A short rest wouldn’t be a bad idea.
“Impressive. Is that the place called ‘Earth’?”
The incarnations gathered companionably together were watching a panel suspended high in the tavern.
It was a recording from the dokkaebis’ [Channels].
I’d thought the scene looked familiar, and a moment later, a familiar voice began to come through.
―Ajusshi!
The scene being shown was from the ‘Seoul Dome Scenario.’ Of all things, it was a recording of the tenth scenario, the ‘73rd Demon King.’
Hearing Shin Yoosung’s voice from the screen made a corner of my heart ache.
I raised my coat collar to cover half my face and watched the recording.
“That scenario really packs a punch. Just like the rumors said, eh?”
“They say that’s the most popular scenario region these days?”
“Those incarnations over there must have it made!”
Almost all mass media in the [Demon Realm] is controlled by Wenny men.

Unlike dokkaebis, Wenny men couldn’t open channels themselves, so they couldn’t earn income through donations. Instead, they made their money by stealing recordings and distributing them throughout the Demon Realm, among other things.
“Fuck, judging by the difficulty, it looks easy as shit. Even I could do that much!”
“Don’t talk nonsense. If you’d gone there, you’d have croaked before even clearing the fifth scenario.”
“Hey, I’m telling you I wouldn’t!”
As the ‘73rd Demon King’ scenario hurtled into its latter stages, the expressions of those grumbling at the screen gradually began to change.
―Uriel, you know. This is just that kind of ‘story.’
It felt truly strange to watch my own lines coming from the screen.
―You’ve seen people die plenty of times by now, haven’t you?
Uriel had been so sad then······.
When I turned my head, several incarnations had tears in their eyes.
Voices of anger, despair, or lament.
“Fuck, this is too sad······.”
······It was an unfamiliar feeling.
The sight of incarnations sympathizing with the story I’d lived through, even though it wasn’t their own scenario. Faces that looked as though they’d received some comfort.
Perhaps constellations weren’t the only ones who needed stories.
Stories were something everyone needed.
“······If we went back to our homeworlds’ scenarios, could we do that much, too?”
“Lampert, do you want to go back?”
“If I could, I wouldn’t mind going.”
“Heh heh, then ask a Wenny man. They’ll send you back anytime.”
“······You call that a joke? I don’t want to become my homeworld’s ‘Disaster.’”
Disaster.
At that word, the atmosphere in the tavern grew tense for an instant.
But only for a very brief moment.
A subject everyone wished to avoid was bound to be dropped quickly.
“Here you are. Food that’s ten times as delicious.”
With a faint smile, I accepted the food.
It consisted of fried morsels coated in snow-white batter and a simple noodle dish. The rich, savory aroma alone told me it was excellent food, even without tasting it.
Looking around with the plate in my hands, I spotted one small head focused on the panel screen like everyone else.
The tearful face of someone who hadn’t even noticed I’d approached.
I clicked my tongue softly and plopped down beside the kid.
“What, does watching it make you homesick?”
“Eek!”
That little startled reaction was adorable.
It was exactly what I’d imagined.
As Jang Hayoung tried to slip away, I pressed gently down on one shoulder.
“Don’t be so wary of me. I just want to share a meal.”

Jang Hayoung eyed me suspiciously, then obediently sat back down beside me. With so many other incarnations around, Hayoung seemed to have decided I wouldn’t do any harm. After some hesitation, Jang Hayoung spoke first.
“Are you done talking with Aileen?”
“Yes.”
“What did you talk about?”
“You don’t need to know.”
“······That’s the special, though.”
“Eat some if you want.”

At my words, Jang Hayoung’s fork flew into action as though the kid had been waiting for the invitation. The heaped noodles disappeared into Jang Hayoung’s mouth before I could even tell where they’d gone.
Come to think of it, [Shamelessness] was one of this kid’s skills, too.
“Well, it’s edible.”
In an instant, Jang Hayoung ate more than half my food.
“······You’re from Earth too, right?”
“Yes.”
My face had never appeared properly on the screen. Perhaps someone had deliberately tampered with the image; my face was distorted as though I’d been punched.
That bastard Bihyung. Why had he edited only my face to look like that?
Anyway, thanks to that, Jang Hayoung seemed unlikely to recognize what I really looked like.
“······What was it like?”
“Terrible.”
Those words alone made Jang Hayoung nod as though understanding everything.
Those who had endured scenarios had little need for elaborate descriptions of tragedy.
“Are you on the screen now, too?”
“I am.”
“Where?”
“There I am now.”
Just then, the screen was showing a close-up of Yoo Joonghyuk’s handsome face. Luckily, the coat I was wearing had become dirty enough to resemble his black coat.
If I insisted convincingly enough, Hayoung might actually believe me······.
But Jang Hayoung’s expression was far from encouraging.
“You don’t look anything alike······.”
“It’s me.”
“No. You look like a lump of pottery clay some random person tried to shape and then squashed, while he looks like a god spent a thousand days······.”
“I’m an exile, remember? The Story around my face collapsed.”
“Even if your Story collapsed, that’s a bit······ At least tell a believable lie.”
······Damn it.
My feelings aside, I still had to accomplish my goal.
“Fine, it’s not me. Still, he looks cool, doesn’t he?”
“Pretty cool.”
“He’s an incredible fighter, too.”
“Really?”
“If you go to Earth, I’ll introduce you. He and I are pretty close.”
At those words, Jang Hayoung’s gaze wavered.
Jang Hayoung would probably have no choice but to take the bait.
In ‘Ways of Survival,’ Jang Hayoung was written as a character who admired Yoo Joonghyuk.
If I took this opportunity to persuade the kid early and encourage a desire to return······.
“Why would I want to meet him?”
“Huh? No, I just······.”
“I’m more interested in that one, actually.”
“Who?”
“That one over there.”
On the screen, I could see a human figure surrounded by pitch-black demonic energy.
A man looking at his companions with sorrowful eyes.
His face wasn’t clearly visible, but I knew very well who he was.
It was me.
Looking at Jang Hayoung’s bright, sparkling eyes, I wondered what on earth was going on.
“You can barely even see his face, though?”
“Why does that matter?”
As I fumbled for words in my confusion, cries suddenly erupted throughout the tavern.
“Waaaaah!”
“No! Open your eyes, Demon King of Salvation!”
“Damn it! I can’t stop crying!”
[Your fame in the 73rd Demon Realm increases.]
[You have obtained 1,500 coins.]
Wait, was I really this popular?
I suddenly began to regret cosplaying as Yoo Joonghyuk.
But I couldn’t tell them now that it was actually me.
―Let’s meet again, Yoo Joonghyuk.
As the scenario finally reached its closing act, people began to wail.
Some were so overwhelmed with emotion that they couldn’t pull themselves out of it.
Jang Hayoung murmured with a rapt expression.
“Ah, I wonder if he already has a girlfriend.”
My heart lurched.
“What? Who?”
“The Demon King of Salvation. Do you happen to know him, too?”
“I do know him, but······.”
I frowned as I looked into Jang Hayoung’s beautiful eyes.
Plump, snow-white cheeks and clear eyes.
In sheer beauty, that face really was extraordinary. But······.
“Aren’t you a guy?”
If I remembered correctly, Jang Hayoung was male.
Because that damned author of ‘Ways of Survival’ had accepted every one of my comments, then changed exactly one thing however they pleased.
And that was this kid’s gender.
Jang Hayoung frowned and said.
“Trying to judge everything by appearances. Typical Earthling.”
Just as I was about to reply, the tavern owner suddenly turned off the lights.
Then he addressed the entire tavern in a very low voice.
“Night is coming.”

At those few quiet words, a deep silence spread through the tavern from the owner outward. A silence far more taut and sharp than when the word ‘Disaster’ had come up earlier. Meeting my eyes, Jang Hayoung put an index finger to their lips.
“Shh.”
Looking more closely, I saw it wasn’t just this tavern.
Other taverns and shops along the street were closing their doors and turning off their lights, too. Sounds were vanishing in an instant.
As though the entire [Industrial Complex] were sinking into the deep sea.
From the deserted street, something like the sound of an eerie flute began to drift in.
I saw several citizens cover their ears to shut out the sound.
At that moment, something came back to me, too.
「A special [Night] comes to the Demon Realm.」
Listening to the [Fourth Wall]’s voice, I recalled the setting of ‘Ways of Survival.’
「All citizens of the [Industrial Complex] fear the nobles. It wasn’t simply because the nobles were strong. It was because of this [Night], which came once every three days.」
“Please just pass us by. Please······.”
Someone murmured those words. How much time passed after that? With a crackling sound as the windows froze over, I sensed something passing along the street.
Sssssss.

Holding their breath, the citizens acted as though they couldn’t see it. Some even bowed their heads all the way down against the tables. The shadow of an enormous scythe, glimpsed now and then beyond the frozen windows.
「When Night falls, an [Executioner] appears in the Industrial Complex.」
「If the citizens have a [Revolutionary], the nobles have an [Executioner].」
The root of the citizens’ inability to resist the nobles despite their terror, and the reason the duke could maintain his position of absolute power in this Industrial Complex.
It all came down to the existence of that [Executioner].
Creeeeak.
The moment the tavern door opened, everyone squeezed their eyes shut.
From the deep darkness came a voice like glass being scratched.
[Who is the Re vo lu tion ar y.]
A body that looked about twice the size of an adult man’s, with an appearance reminiscent of the Grim Reaper.
The black cape draped over it concealed its face, but the sinister aura it exuded was enough for me to sense its power.
[The target is currently under the protection of the scenario.]
[The target is currently invincible.]
No being could stand against that [Executioner] inside the [Industrial Complex] at Night.
The owner who had served me food and the people who had noisily chatted while watching the scenario were all staring at the floor, their faces deathly pale.
Tonight, the [Executioner] had chosen this tavern as its execution ground.
Someone here would certainly die in this very place tonight.
[Who is the Re vo lu tion ar y.]
People curled in on themselves whenever the Executioner’s scythe swept past them. It looked almost like a game. As I studied the creature closely, Jang Hayoung tugged at my collar in alarm.
“Don’t make eye contact.”
At that faint sound, the [Executioner] turned toward us.
More precisely, toward Jang Hayoung, who was swearing.
Watching the [Executioner] slowly approach, Jang Hayoung began to tremble.
The face of someone sensing their own impending death.
I planted a hand on the utterly terrified Jang Hayoung’s head and slowly rose from my seat.
Leaving Jang Hayoung gaping in shock, I raised my head. The [Executioner] was watching me with ominous eyes.
「Kim Dokja thought. What would Yoo Joonghyuk have done?」
He would never have revealed himself here.
Yoo Joonghyuk would have kept himself hidden to the very end, looking for the situation that would benefit him most.
