Honestly, this damned <Star Stream> had no consideration for newbies.
We were so desperately asking for help, yet not a single person had sent a reply.
After that, we wrote and sent several more messages.
[I’m looking for someone who can make me a ‘Fighter.’]
[I need your ‘Fighter’ skill.]
[Please help me.]
But no matter how many messages we sent, no reply came.
They probably thought it was spam and were ignoring it······ Damn it.
Since I had no talent for writing, I had absolutely no idea what kind of message would get a reply.
A shame Han Sooyoung wasn’t here at a time like this.
She would have come up with a good idea.
After thinking for a moment with furrowed brows, Jang Hayoung spoke.
“······We just need to get a reply first, right? Can I try writing whatever I want?”
“Have you thought of something?”
Jang Hayoung gave a small nod and typed a message.
[I’m a fifteen-year-old middle school girl.]
“Hey, wait―”
But before I could stop it, Jang Hayoung pressed the send button.
[No recipient was entered. The message has been sent to random constellations.]
It was not even addressed to anyone in particular.
I shouted in exasperation.
“These are constellations we’re dealing with! How could something like that possibly work?”
“······Just wait.”
What on earth was wrong with this kid······.
But the next moment.
[A reply has arrived!]
We looked at each other blankly, then checked the reply.
Surprisingly, the constellation who had replied was one I knew.
[Sender ― Abyssal Black Flame Dragon].
Once Jang Hayoung started talking in earnest with the ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon,’ Hayoung began grinning away. What was so entertaining? I watched, then offered a mild rebuke.
“What’s so funny?”
“It’s just the way he talks.”
Jang Hayoung was strange enough for talking about that exalted great constellation as though he were a friend, but the Abyssal Black Flame Dragon who had sent the reply was even more ridiculous.
Why was this bastard replying to random messages instead of paying attention to Han Sooyoung?
Then Jang Hayoung shook their head, as though defending the Black Flame Dragon.
“I don’t think he’s as bad as you think.”
“What nonsense is that? Has he already won you over?”
“He’s more of a gentleman when he talks than I expected, too.”
“A gentleman? What kind of gentleman replies to ‘I’m a fifteen-year-old middle school girl’?”
I was about to snap that surely I did not need to spell out the sordid implications when Jang Hayoung answered.
“He says he only replied because I’m fifteen.”
“What? He replied because you’re fifteen? What a complete piece of shit.”
I had known the Abyssal Black Flame Dragon was cruel and out of his mind, but learning his tastes ran that way suddenly made me a little worried about Han Sooyoung.
“Why are you getting so worked up? He says he’s just happy to have a friend. He’s fifteen, too.”
“What bullshit! I don’t know how old he really is, but how could there possibly be a fifteen-year-old constellation?”
And at that moment, a detail of the setting suddenly came back to me.

「Constellations living within the age-old flow of the <Star Stream> are accustomed to confining themselves within fixed frameworks to preserve their sense of self. A typical example is ‘age’: they tend to identify with a particular age of a particular life-form and think of themselves as being that age.」
······Could it be?
But even so, identifying with a fifteen-year-old? Seriously?
―Aaaaaaaargh!
That was when a scream came from inside the treatment room.
It was Han Myungoh’s.
Turning toward it, I spoke to the startled Jang Hayoung.
“Keep talking for a bit. I’ll be right back.”
“Okay. What should I ask?”
“Just leave him alone. He isn’t a [Fighter] anyway. Talk to someone else instead. You have that list I gave you earlier, right? Try contacting them again.”
Jang Hayoung nodded.
That somehow delighted expression made me uneasy, but I figured it would be fine. It was Hayoung’s own ability, after all.

The ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ had awakened a little earlier than in the original novel, but for now, this was the best option. Without the wall’s help, revolution in the [Industrial Complex] would be impossible.
When I opened the treatment room door, the now-awake Han Myungoh was looking at me in a cold sweat.
“Why did I pass out?”
I quietly closed the treatment room door and answered.
“You fainted while remembering the pain of childbirth.”
Perhaps he had had a nightmare while unconscious; sweat was pouring down Han Myungoh’s forehead.
“Was that all?”
“I think you cursed Asmodeus a little, too.”
“That son of a bitch······.”
He was also expressing his hatred for the Demon King more openly than before.
Normally, that would have been dangerous. But with the power of the [Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword] keeping us out of Asmodeus’s sight, a little swearing would not kill him.
I pulled up a chair again and sat down.
“Let’s hear it again. What was that about giving birth, and why did Asmodeus favor you?”
“······First, I need to explain why I became pregnant.”
“I can more or less guess. Wasn’t it because of the ‘Dark Keeper’ we fought before?”

Just before we parted, Han Myungoh had been parasitized by the tentacles of the [Dark Keeper] in the [Dark Fold]. Normally, that did not immediately make someone conceive a demon, but it seemed to have worked instantly on Han Myungoh.
“That was the trigger. But it wasn’t what made me pregnant.”
“It was the curse.”

Back then, Han Myungoh had contributed to the final blow against the ‘Dark Keeper’ and received ‘Asmodeus’s’ curse. Asmodeus’s curse consumed probability to bring about whatever its target considered ‘the most terrible thing.’ In other words······.
“I see. But is that possible? Giving birth in a male body······.”
“Please don’t ask me about that part.”
I gave a small nod.
It was the least respect I could show an older man who had undergone an unbelievable experience.
We were silent for a while.
All at once, talking with Han Myungoh like this felt unfamiliar.
「Kim Dokja thought. What a strange feeling.」

Before the apocalypse, when I had been ‘Kim Dokja, office worker,’ Han Myungoh had simply been someone I found difficult to deal with. One of the bosses I most wanted to avoid. Those days had certainly existed. Days when a 3,000-won convenience-store lunch could lift or crush my spirits, and I had to count out my remaining youth in the pay slips that arrived each month.
But those days were all gone.
And now Kim Dokja and Han Myungoh, no longer employee and department manager, were sitting together and talking about a ‘Demon King.’
“Kim Dok······ no, Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi. Do you know what it means to become a father?”
Han Myungoh’s sudden question caught me a little off guard.
“Of course I don’t.”
“Now I do.”
Truthfully, I found it difficult to decide whether Han Myungoh should be called a father or a mother, but it was not important, so I let it go. Department Manager Han Myungoh’s face was serious.
“It was painful.”
Those words sounded far more painful than the hundred bits of nonsense Han Myungoh had spouted until now.
“And I was happy.”
I was surprised Han Myungoh could make an expression like that.
And in that moment, I realized what the unfamiliar emotion I had been feeling was.
Perhaps I had not wanted to admit it.
Everyone changes. Good or evil, child or adult.
“My daughter was very beautiful.”
“I’d like to meet her. Is she here in the Demon Realm?”
“She isn’t with me now.”
Watching his expression quickly darken, I had a premonition.
“It’s a long story. Will you hear me out?”
“Go ahead. I like listening to stories.”
Han Myungoh had not become the ‘Demon King’s’ subordinate right away.
Somewhere my companions and I knew nothing about, Han Myungoh’s tenacious story had continued.
Taking the daughter he had given birth to with him, he had fought his way through the scenarios alone.
Through the Struggle for the Flag.
Through the War of Kings.
Through the five disasters.

I could hardly believe that a story like that had been unfolding somewhere I could not see. I could not believe that Han Myungoh, of all people, could devote himself to someone like that. Yet, at the same time, I could not deny it.
Just as I was no longer the Kim Dokja I used to be.
The man before me was no longer the old Han Myungoh, either.
I did not know whether giving birth had been what brought it about.
But one thing was certain: he, too, had changed.
“It must have been difficult.”
“It was. I nearly died many times. In fact, at the very end, I found myself in a truly hopeless predicament.”

He had finally been driven to the edge when he became caught up in the [Dark Castle] scenario, which had not even officially begun at the time. Surrounded by swarming demons and demon nobles, Han Myungoh realized he could no longer protect his child.
For the first time in his life, Han Myungoh prayed.
If someone would protect this child.
If they would only save this child, he would do anything.
And, surprisingly, a being answered that prayer.
―What a beautiful child.
“It was Asmodeus.”
“······Don’t tell me the Demon King took your child?”
For a moment, an unsettling image came to mind, leaving me sickened.
Asmodeus was the Demon King of wrath and lust.
If a child had fallen into his hands, what would become of her was painfully obvious. Yet Han Myungoh’s expression was calm.
“The child should be safe. She was born from ‘Asmodeus’s’ curse, after all. And······ fortunately or unfortunately, the Demon King is in no position to lay a hand on my daughter.”
“What does that mean?”
“The Demon King made my daughter his ‘incarnation body.’”
Only then did I think I understood what had happened.
Whatever whim had prompted it, Demon King ‘Asmodeus’ had made Han Myungoh’s child his incarnation body. Naturally, then, Han Myungoh, as the child’s parent, would have received a demon noble’s title.
“······That is why I became a ‘demon.’”

Hearing this much, I thought Han Myungoh’s life had been quite a journey. Should I call it a successful life because he had received a noble title, or a failed one because his child had been taken from him······.
That was when Han Myungoh, his eyes heavy with grief, spoke again.
“I want to rescue my daughter.”
For a moment, I thought I had misheard.
He wanted to do what?
“I won’t waste words. Please help me. Help me just this once, and I will never forget what you’ve done for me.”
I wondered what on earth this sudden turn of events was.
After starring in his own little human-interest documentary, now he wanted my help?
“You’ve watched me for a long time, so you know me well. I’m the kind of man who can be endlessly cowardly if he chooses. But even I have things I cannot give up.”

“And what happened last night was beyond my expectations. I told them only to frighten people, never to hurt them. When the Guardian suddenly appeared, the Executioners got worked up and acted on their own.”
I could not tell whether he was lying.
For the moment, I responded rationally.
“I’m sorry, but I have no plans to fight Asmodeus.”
Making an enemy of one of the 72 Demon Kings now would complicate matters.
It would mean drawing in a foreign power before the revolution had even begun.
But Han Myungoh’s response was unexpected.
“You don’t need to fight Asmodeus. Just do what you were planning to do. Start a revolution and kill the duke. That will help me.”
“······Weren’t you on the duke’s side?”
“Originally, yes. But now that things have turned out this way, I think helping you might be a good option, too.”
“What do you mean?”
“Asmodeus never wanted me to help the duke in the first place. He made me an offer. If I created a ‘Story’ he wanted, he would return my daughter. That was why I attached myself to ‘Duke Syswitz.’”
This part of the story had been completely absent from the original novel.
Of course it had. ‘Han Myungoh’ had not existed in the original novel to begin with.
After thinking for a moment, I asked,
“What exactly is the story the Demon King wants?”
“The king of the 73rd Demon Realm.”
Han Myungoh slowly raised his head and looked at me.
I remembered the look in Han Myungoh’s eyes when he had interviewed me back when I first joined ‘Mino Soft.’
“The Demon King······ told me to create the ‘king of the 73rd Demon Realm’ with my own hands.”
Yoo Joonghyuk was gazing at the night sky with impassive eyes.

A sky with constellations different from Earth’s. Leaning at an angle against the Splitting the Sky Sword and counting those stars, Yoo Joonghyuk was far more exhausted than usual. A body drenched in blood, a face covered in wounds. Before him lay the grade 2 monster he had just beaten down.
“······That finishes the 15th scenario, too.”
Planet Lugratia.
Yoo Joonghyuk had come here through a ‘personal scenario’ commissioned by one of the constellations of another world.

Normally, he would have been working through Earth’s scenarios, but in this life he had strong companions on Earth, so he had decided it might not be a bad idea to leave the scenarios in the 10s to others. He was already growing faster than in his previous round, anyway. It was best to build up as much strength as possible while he could. Once the scenarios entered the 20s, he would no longer have this kind of leeway.
‘I have to become stronger.’

With that single thought, Yoo Joonghyuk had been replacing main scenarios with ‘personal scenarios’ ever since scenario 11. He chose only the most difficult personal scenarios with the best rewards. At times, he even took on scenarios that were reckless undertakings by his usual standards.
Fighting, fighting, and fighting again.

As always, he believed that pushing his body to its limits and tempering his mind would be enough. He thought it would fill at least a little of this inexplicable sense of loss. Yet, strangely, the more he fought, the greater the emptiness became.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ looks at you with sorrow.]
Yoo Joonghyuk frowned and glared at the sky.

Demon-like Judge of Fire. Yoo Joonghyuk could not quite understand why that constellation had been speaking to him so often lately. In the previous round, they had barely had anything to do with each other······.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ asks why you are not looking for Kim Dokja.]
“Kim Dokja is dead.”
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ shakes her head with tears welling in her eyes.]
Yoo Joonghyuk could not understand why a constellation would be so troubled by the death of a mere incarnation.
The next message was even harder to understand.
[Your notoriety is increasing in the 73rd Demon Realm.]
‘Again?’
A message that appeared whenever he was about to forget it.

No matter how much he thought about it, Yoo Joonghyuk could not understand why his notoriety was increasing in some unrelated place like the 73rd Demon Realm. At first, he had wondered whether Kim Dokja might be alive and impersonating him, but even if Kim Dokja were alive, that bastard would have no reason to······.
‘······Wait. What if Kim Dokja is alive and in danger?’
Perhaps Kim Dokja was alive.
Perhaps he had escaped that damned fate and was living alone out on the Story Horizon, where there were no scenarios.
Having survived that way.
Perhaps he was asking for help.
That guy, who had always outpaced him with outlandish tricks, was in danger for the first time and asking for help.
But there was no way to ask for help in a place without a channel······.
Having thought that far, Yoo Joonghyuk looked up at the sky again, his expression a little more complicated.
‘The 73rd Demon Realm······.’
「Kim Dokja thought. I wonder if everyone is doing well.」
I had hoped the screen panel might bring me news of Earth again, but no footage appeared. Well, even the Wenny men probably couldn’t steal footage from the dokkaebis’ channels that easily.
Night was fast approaching.
I had barely slept properly for days, but thanks to Aileen repairing my Stories whenever she could, my incarnation body wasn’t in such bad condition.
“I’ve patched you up for now, but you need to be careful when you go out. You know that, right? You’re still someone who’s been expelled from the main scenario.”
“You sound just like a doctor.”
“I’m not working on a clock right now, so I can hardly talk like a clockmaker, can I?”
Aileen shot me a look and stood up with her repair tools.
Despite everything that had happened in those two days, she didn’t seem particularly unhappy with the current situation.
「Kim Dokja thought. If I hadn’t come, Aileen would have gone on living as a clockmaker.」

In the many rounds when Yoo Joonghyuk hadn’t come to the Demon Realm, Aileen must indeed have lived that way. Quietly making clocks that told the time back home, reflecting alone on the time of a vanished planet. Occasionally bickering with Jang Hayoung and eating the food Mark made······ Perhaps that would have been a happier life for Aileen.
“You know what? More people have been coming for clocks these past two days.”
When I glanced up, Aileen was watching me with an unreadable look.
I hesitated for a moment before asking,
“Did everyone’s clocks break at once or something?”
“People in the [Industrial Complex] never used clocks before.”
“Why?”
“Because knowing the time was of no use to them.”
I remembered reading about it in ‘Ways of Survival,’ too.
I also remembered that someone had called the Demon Realm ‘the city that lost its time’ for that very reason.
“But shouldn’t they at least know when [Night] is coming?”
“Could knowing when [Night] comes change the fact that they’re fated to die?”
A fear that has lasted too long becomes a law.
For a very long time, [Night] had been a natural part of this [Industrial Complex].
Once every three days, someone died, and their Stories were used as fertilizer for the factory.
Regardless of what kind of life they had lived, what stories they had, or what tomorrow they would have lived to see.
And the others lived another three days with someone missing.
“But then a [Night] came when no one died. Because of you.”

“People can ‘fear’ the night again. They’ve begun to think that it might be something they can solve, rather than something natural. That perhaps they can live with tomorrow in mind. That’s what they’ve begun to think.”
When I happened to lower my gaze, I saw that Aileen, too, was wearing a watch.
There were now three hours until tonight’s [Night]······.
Aileen and I fell silent, listening to the ticking of the second hand.
Some people in the [Industrial Complex] were probably watching their clocks now, just as we were.
Tonight would probably be fiercer and harder than last night.
And yet, why was it? Just listening to the diligent ticking of the second hand made me feel a little comforted.
Even though I wasn’t the one who needed comforting.
“Thank you.”
“······I didn’t tell you all that just to make you feel better. It’s just that a gloomy Revolutionary isn’t a pleasant sight.”
Aileen abruptly turned away. I gave her a wry smile, then hurriedly added,
“Ah, wait a moment.”
“······What is it?”
“Speaking of clocks, do you know how to make other things?”
“What other things?”
“A smartphone······ I suppose you’d call it.”
“What’s that? A magical device?”
After wondering how to explain it, I gave her a rough description of a smartphone’s features. Then Aileen spoke as though she understood.
“So it’s a sort of communication device? With a little panel?”
“That’s right.”
“But there aren’t any dokkaebi channels here, so communication shouldn’t be possible······.”
Anyway, judging by my past experience, it didn’t really matter whether there was a connection. A phone in my hands would synchronize automatically and generate the text file anyway.
“Don’t worry about that. Can you make it today?”
“One day is impossible. I think it’ll take at least three days······ But I’ll give it a try.”
“All right. I’ll leave it to you, then.”

With that, I left Aileen’s workshop and headed toward the tavern. I could feel people watching me with curious looks when they spotted me in the street. Some acknowledged me with a glance, while others lightly clasped their hands together. And, just as Aileen had said, each of them wore a watch on their wrist.

「Looking at those watches, Yoo Joonghyuk grew lonely. They had recovered their time, but he still wasn’t living in this time. A thought suddenly occurred to Yoo Joonghyuk. Then which of those countless times am I living in?」
It was a monologue by Yoo Joonghyuk, who had once saved the Demon Realm.
And it was one of my favorite scenes in ‘Ways of Survival.’
Suddenly, I felt I understood a little of what he felt, if only a little.
For the regressor Yoo Joonghyuk, the time of all these worlds was not his own. In a life where he could regress again and again, there was no way the present time could hold any meaning······.
When this was over, perhaps I would ask Aileen to make a watch.
Even something like that might help him grow more attached to this world.
Perhaps his Regression Depression might improve a little, too······.
I knew this world wouldn’t disappear if he regressed, but even so, clearing the remaining scenarios would be difficult without him.
“Ahahahaha, this guy’s hilarious.”
When I opened the tavern door, I saw Jang Hayoung laughing away. Seen only from this far away, Hayoung looked like an ordinary middle school kid going through puberty.
“What are you doing?”
There was no “Eek” this time. Instead, Jang Hayoung avoided my eyes like a child caught doing something bad by a parent.
“I-I was doing what you told me to!”
“What about the [Fighter]?”
Jang Hayoung fumbled for words, lips moving for a moment, before finally admitting the truth.
“······None of the [Fighters] replied?”
“I-It’s true! Not one of them sent a reply!”
“What on earth did you send them?”
“I’m a fifteen-year-old middle school girl······.”
A vein throbbed in my forehead.
“Hey! Of course no one’s replying if that’s what you sent!”
“But it worked earlier······.”
“Do you think they’re all like the Black Flame Dragon? How many did you send?”
“About 300 altogether······.”
It occurred to me that they might have thought it was spam and blocked the messages. Damn it.
“This is bad. That was the entire list of [Fighters] I know.”
Only then did Jang Hayoung’s expression change, as though finally realizing how much trouble we were in.
“Then what do we do now?”
This was why I needed ‘Ways of Survival.’
If I had the text file, I could have reread the parts I hadn’t examined closely and searched for more information on [Fighters].
“We’ll have to look for another [Fighter]. For now······.”
I called to mind a few constellation modifiers that immediately occurred to me.
Someone among the constellations who might help us.
“Try writing to the ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband.’”
“······Isn’t that an incredibly powerful constellation?”
I didn’t know whether he had any skills related to the [Fighter].
Still, we were at the point where we had to grasp at straws.
Jang Hayoung busily typed out a message.
And we waited. 1 minute, 2 minutes······ 5 minutes.
Jang Hayoung shook their head.
“There’s no reply.”
“Try writing this.”
I dictated another message.
Jang Hayoung started in alarm.
“Can we really send something like that?”
“We have to get his attention first.”
The Great Sage, Heaven’s Equal was lazy by nature. It would take at least this much to get a reply from him.
Not even 10 seconds after Jang Hayoung sent the message, a notification appeared.
[A reply has arrived!]
“H-He replied!”
“Just as I thought, right?”
For reference, the message I had told Hayoung to send was as follows.
[Grow, grow, hair, hair]
His indirect messages had him pulling out his hair every time I did anything, so I’d wondered. Sure enough, it seemed he’d started losing his hair. I asked,
“What did he say?”
“He says he’ll kill me if we ever meet.”
“Anything else?”
“He’s asking who I am. Should I say Yoo Joonghyuk?”
“······Don’t answer.”
Saying Yoo Joonghyuk would be funny, but it would only stir up needless trouble.
I rubbed my temples and thought hard.
The Great Sage, Heaven’s Equal seemed to be a lost cause, so I had to find another way out.
“Demon-like Judge of Fire······ Calling her from the Demon Realm would be a little awkward. Or Secretive Plotter······ I still don’t know who that one is······.”
It was a difficult choice.
“With the ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ or the ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy,’ there’s Olympus to worry about······.”
If I simply revealed that I was alive, I felt that at least one of them might help. The problem was that revealing my identity would also let those nebula bastards discover that I had survived.
“This is tricky.”
It was the first impasse I had encountered since entering the Demon Realm.
There wasn’t much time left until [Night].
If Jang Hayoung couldn’t inherit the [Fighter] now, all my plans for tonight would come to nothing.
Then Jang Hayoung spoke.
“Flamy says he can help.”
I paused for a moment, wondering who on earth ‘Flamy’ was supposed to be.
“······You’re still talking to that guy?”
“Yeah.”
“Forget him. He’s bound to be all talk.”
“No, he says he was a [Fighter] in the Demon Realm for a little while, too.”
······The Abyssal Black Flame Dragon had once been a [Fighter]?
Nothing like that had ever appeared in ‘Ways of Survival.’
Well, thinking about it, the Abyssal Black Flame Dragon had never been covered in much depth, so it wasn’t impossible······.
“But he says he didn’t like the scenario rules, so he killed everyone.”
“What?”
“He says he killed them all—the duke, the Revolutionary, the Executioners.”
Something suddenly came to mind.
Was it perhaps when the 64th Demon Realm was unified?
I did seem to remember a lunatic like that somewhere in the Demon Realm’s history.
But that had been the ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’?
“Ask if he can pass on the [Fighter] skill.”

The Abyssal Black Flame Dragon was an evil-aligned constellation, so he probably wouldn’t have to worry much about others’ reactions to sending something to the Demon Realm. If we could get his help, he was the ideal choice.
I saw Jang Hayoung’s face brighten suddenly as they typed something.
“He says giving it away isn’t a problem, since he doesn’t use it anyway.”
“Really?”
······It was truly unexpected help.
Could this problem be solved in a way I’d never even imagined?
It was enough to make me wonder whether the Black Flame Dragon and Kim Namwoon had both actually been decent guys. Once I got the text file again, I’d have to read their parts carefully.
But Jang Hayoung wasn’t finished.
“But he says there’s one condition.”
Of course there was.
There was no way that cantankerous bastard would just give it away.
“Trades through the wall require payment anyway. What’s his condition?”
“He says something’s been bothering him lately.”
“Bothering him?”
“He’s not getting along very well with his incarnation······.”
“His incarnation?”
“He says his incarnation keeps ignoring him.”
The Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’s incarnation would be······.
“He says his incarnation won’t even consider listening to him, despite being in danger right now······.”
······In danger?
I quickly cut Jang Hayoung off and asked,
“Tell him to explain that in detail.”
Shuuunk!
With the sound of a blade piercing a heart, the last man fell.
“Ghk, ugh······ You, you fucking······.”
He tried desperately to force out a curse, but a back kick from the woman crushed his mouth. That was the end of him.
Han Sooyoung surveyed the office, now a sea of blood.
“······Finally killed them all. Korean bastards adapt so fucking fast.”
This was the headquarters of ‘Survival of the Fittest,’ an incarnation club in Gyeonggi Province.

Bastards who had turned into a criminal gang as soon as the scenarios began and they chose reasonably useful constellation sponsors. They had even rejected government control, and if they weren’t killed now, they would later become a cancer on the Korean Peninsula.
That was what they were going to become, as far as the original novel was concerned.
“Damn you, Kim Dokja.”
She let loose a torrent of curses, but it still didn’t make her feel any better.
So Han Sooyoung added one more.
“Yoo Joonghyuk, you son of a bitch.”
Thinking of those two bastards, who had dumped this place on her and gone their separate ways, Han Sooyoung felt like a food-waste disposal crew left to deal with their discarded leftovers.
“Damn it. Kim Dokja aside, what the hell is wrong with that bastard Yoo Joonghyuk?”

Whatever the hell had gotten into him, Yoo Joonghyuk had started doing things he’d never done in the original third round as soon as he left the Seoul Dome. Holing up in a corner of his room, muttering endlessly to himself, then suddenly abandoning the Korean Peninsula’s scenarios and leaving for a ‘personal scenario’······.
Thanks to that, every last scrap of their leftovers had become Han Sooyoung’s responsibility.
“What’s the point of thinking about it any more? Fu······.”
After all, she was also the ‘Last Person to Get Off’ who had read Ways of Survival.
With both Kim Dokja and Yoo Joonghyuk gone, she was naturally the only person left who could take responsibility for the Korean Peninsula.
She was about to slip quietly away from the scene of the massacre, heaving sigh after sigh, when.
“Oh, you startled me. What brings you here?”
A woman was waiting for her, leaning against the office doorway.
A suit-like combat outfit clinging to her entire body, hair flowing freely. A loose coat draped over her shoulders, perhaps out of awareness of how much her figure showed.
It struck her anew: that really was a beautiful face.
Well, that was probably why the media made such a fuss over her.

Syswitz's [Factory].

The horizon near the Syswitz Industrial Complex.
