It was the moment when information about the final chapter, veiled for so long, finally revealed itself before my eyes.
After the Demon King Selection ended, the ‘Yoo Joonghyuk―Kim Dokja Industrial Complex’ became busy with reconstruction.

The citizens faced the prospect of homelessness in the aftermath of the war, and their faces were bleak. If not for the relief supplies I had persuaded Bihyung to provide, the mood would have been even uglier.
“The clock tower goes over there! Hey, watch out!”

With the dukes dead, citizens from other industrial complexes arrived in an endless stream, so there was no shortage of labor. I spent two days helping the citizens rebuild, and the city was gradually regaining its vitality.
“Thank you for helping, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
Without Yoo Sangah’s [Arachne’s Web], the initial reconstruction would have taken much longer. Wiping the sweat from her forehead, Yoo Sangah said,
“……You should get some rest too, Dokja-ssi.”
“I’m fine. How about you, Yoo Sangah-ssi?”
Yoo Sangah studied the bandages wrapped around my chest before answering.
“I’m in good condition too.”
Good condition……
Somehow, that choice of words was very like Yoo Sangah.
I stopped working and climbed the clock tower with Yoo Sangah to look down over the square.

Yoo Joonghyuk and the other seriously injured members of our group were hospitalized in Aileen’s ward. Jung Heewon and Lee Jihye, whose injuries had been relatively minor, were helping with construction near the entrance to the complex. From the ward, I could hear Lee Hyunsung stubbornly insisting that he was all better and would be checking out.
Perhaps thanks to two days of hard work, at least the area around the square was beginning to look like a place people lived.
The schedule was tight, but pushing ourselves now would pay off later.
“Here they come.”
A portal shimmering in midair.
A little kid was racing toward us from the square at incredible speed.
I lightly jumped down from the clock tower to greet him.
“Dokja hyung! Waaaaaaah!”
Lee Gilyoung threw himself into my arms and squirmed against me. I smiled and ruffled his hair.
“Been doing well? Looks like you’ve grown a little.”
“Really?”
“Yeah. You must be almost as tall as Yoosung now.”
“I’ll be taller soon!”
Lee Gilyoung wasn’t the only one who had come through the portal in midair. A large man landed in the square with a thud.
“It’s been a while, Gong Pildu-ssi.”
“……Hmph.”

As though he had no interest whatsoever in my well-being, Gong Pildu glared at me briefly before giving Yoo Sangah a small wave. When she bowed her head with a faint smile, his mood seemed to improve a little.
“I didn’t come to see you, you bastard.”
Still, even this showed how much Gong Pildu had changed.
Who could call him one of the Ten Evils now?
“Where’s Han Sooyoung?”
“Sooyoung noona said she thinks she’ll need to recuperate for a while.”
Lee Gilyoung spoke as he lightly bumped his forehead against my stomach.
Recuperate……
Even if she had offered up [Abyss Stones], having the Black Flame Dragon descend into her body while bearing the probability cost must have taken a considerable toll.
But surely it couldn’t be bad enough to keep her from coming here……
“Oh, Sooyoung noona told me to give you this.”
Lee Gilyoung rummaged through his pocket and handed me a note.
True to Han Sooyoung, it had been folded over and over with an oddly obsessive persistence.
Shielding it from Lee Gilyoung’s sparkling eyes, I carefully opened the note.
―Make me do this shit again and I’ll kill you.
A chuckle escaped me.
Just as I thought. She had a reason for not coming.
Even now, closing my eyes brought back the image of Han Sooyoung wrapped in bandages and rampaging like a crazy bitch.
―There are still a few problems left.

The note contained some other information as well. Things you could only hear about on Earth, such as the situation on the Korean Peninsula and relations between nebulae. Fortunately, Earth didn’t seem to have strayed far from the cycle of events in the original novel I knew. In fact, I already knew most of it, so there was no need for her to pass it along like this.
Perhaps Han Sooyoung knew that too, because she kept rambling and repeating herself.
―Anyway, that’s how it is…… Well…… Take care, idiot. See you when you get to Earth.
What a shame. I’d been planning to really tease her when we met this time.
I put the note inside my coat and addressed Lee Gilyoung and Gong Pildu.
“There will be a banquet tonight. Go inside, wash up, and get ready.”
“A banquet?”
“We’re expecting some guests.”
We had made it through one crisis for now.
But this industrial complex’s troubles were only just beginning.
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ accepts your invitation.]
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ accepts your invitation.]
Watching the countless indirect messages pouring out of the air, I let out a small sigh.
Yoo Joonghyuk still hadn’t woken up since the selection.
“How much longer will it take him to recover?”
“He’ll need at least another 2 weeks.”
After checking Yoo Joonghyuk’s pulse, Aileen glanced at me on her way out of the room.
“……And you need some rest too. You know that, right?”
“Don’t worry.”
Even after Aileen left, I stayed in Yoo Joonghyuk’s room.

His sleeping face was paler than that of any ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ I had ever seen. Naturally. This was the first Yoo Joonghyuk who hadn’t gone back despite suffering injuries serious enough to activate ‘Regression.’
I stood up and checked the Story packs connected to him.
Hooking up the wrong Story pack could even cause fatal side effects from having to endure the cringe (降魔).
It was a little different if you had [Lamarck’s Giraffe], like me……
“……Even the packs he uses are just like him.”
「Here I Come, You Lonely World」
「Becoming a Sword Master Was the Easiest Part」
「I’ve Wielded a Sword Since I Was Five—I Was a Genius」

Fortunately, Aileen, a Story Expert, seemed to have a good grasp of Yoo Joonghyuk’s Story composition. In fact, the Yoo Joonghyuk of the 144th round had once briefly gone mad after mistakenly receiving a transfusion of Lee Hyunsung’s military Story.
“He’s a picky eater.”
The voice that suddenly came from behind me startled me so badly that I nearly had a fit.
When I turned, a beautiful giant was leaning against the wall.
“……How long have you been there?”
“Since before you came in.”
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint looked down at me calmly, then glanced at Yoo Joonghyuk.
“This treatment is excessive. Toss him a few Murim dumplings and he’d be better in no time.”
“We don’t have any Murim dumplings here.”
Despite her words, the look in the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s eyes was exceedingly gentle.
That was when a fearsome man’s voice rang out.
“So, is that the bastard who hit you?”
Something the size of a frog was clinging upside down to the ceiling opposite the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
It was Kyrgios Rodgraim.
“Master.”
“Tell me. Was it him?”

Come to think of it, I remembered the nonsense I’d spouted when I sent Kyrgios to Murim. Hadn’t I said the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s disciple had beaten me up? Kyrgios’s handsome brows curved, and the aura of [Electrification] began to envelop his entire body.
“Was it all a lie?”
I swallowed and scrambled for something to say.
“Well, it wasn’t entirely a lie! We’re actually on pretty bad terms. He really has beaten me up before……”
“Were you only on the receiving end?”
“Of course, I’ve hit him too……”

Though I had exploited a loophole in the system, I had beaten Yoo Joonghyuk to a bloody pulp during the struggle for the throne, so it wasn’t a lie. A flicker of interest crossed the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s face as she listened.
“Hmm. You hit my disciple?”
“So who won?”
The two masters’ gazes clashed in midair.
Their eyes had merely met, yet my perception of space warped and sparks began to fly.
Since the two had come back together, I’d assumed their relationship must have improved. Apparently, that had been wishful thinking. The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint spoke in an icy voice.
“What a foolish question. One look at their faces makes it obvious that my disciple is a cut above yours.”
“My disciple could never be weaker than a pretty boy who’s done nothing but build muscle. He may not look it, but I’ve passed down my secret martial art to him……”
“And I’m sure it’s just another martial art that makes you smaller.”
Bzzzzzzzt!
At this rate, the hospital room looked likely to explode, so I quickly stepped between them.
“There’s something I’d like to ask you both.”
Two terrifying gazes fell on me at once. I activated my ‘Status’ and barely withstood the pressure as I asked,
“What happened to <First Murim>?”
It was a question I’d been wondering about all along.
Since the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and Kyrgios had come here, I knew Murim was probably safe. Still, their opponent had been an ‘Outer God.’
Kyrgios was the first to speak.
“Hmph. I went there in person. Do you think I couldn’t save a single world like that?”
With that, Kyrgios flew straight out the window, as though something had offended him.
……What was his problem?
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint quietly watched the window Kyrgios had flown through before speaking.
“We did stop it, but it’s hard to say we stopped everything.”
“Did you defeat the ‘Outer God’?”
The faint presence of a ‘Giant Story’ emanating from the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s entire body.
It was probably a Giant Story connected to <First Murim>. It had to be.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint gave a slight nod.
“It was a formidable opponent, but not beyond us. That obnoxious Paradox bastard came to help, after all.”
Only someone on the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s level could describe an Outer God as merely a ‘formidable opponent.’
“The problem was the one that came after it.”
Even Outer Gods had ranks.
In other words, there were named ones among them too.
For example, the gods collectively known as ‘Old Ones’ or ‘Great Old Ones.’
―It was neither an ‘Old One’ nor a ‘Great Old One.’
But among them were unfathomable beings that transcended even those categories.

―I’d never seen anything like it, so I can’t give you a clear explanation of what it was. What I can say for certain is that even Paradox and I together were no match for it. In fact, it wasn’t even a fight. If it hadn’t withdrawn of its own accord, we would have vanished from the universe along with Murim.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s words sounded downright strange.

According to the original novel’s events, there was absolutely no probability that would allow a god like that to appear in <First Murim> that day. Yet such an immense god had appeared, then withdrawn just as inexplicably.
―It vanished as though it had found some other delicious prey.
A being that was neither an Old One nor a Great Old One.
A god so powerful that merely looking at it made mighty figures like the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and the White Snow of Pitch freeze and lose the will to fight……
Waaaaaah!
A modest party was underway in the [Industrial Complex]’s central hall. Some of my companions had recovered. I could also see the symbolic bodies of several invited constellations.
[Hmm, Demon King of Salvation. Did you receive the gift I sent?]

Persephone approached with a mischievous smile. As expected, her symbolic body looked like Yoo Sangah again. My companions, seeing her symbolic body for the first time, looked startled. Yoo Sangah’s expression in particular was quite a sight.
“……I don’t like garter belts anymore.”
Dressed in a cheongsam, Persephone laughed and waved her fan.
[Really? I sent one with quite good performance.]
At the word ‘performance,’ I saw Lee Hyunsung perk up beside me.
I quickly spoke before he could say anything outlandish.
“I’m indebted to you for your help during the selection.”
[Hmm, but I didn’t do anything.]
“I know you persuaded the ‘Master of the Skywalk.’”
<Olympus> was currently divided. If she hadn’t persuaded Hermes, I might have had to fight even more constellations from <Olympus> during the selection.
[Think of it as an investment in the future.]

With a faint smile, Persephone went to the center of the hall and began to dance, apparently in a good mood. She even pulled Yoo Sangah in to be her partner. Though flustered at first, Yoo Sangah soon maintained a cool expression, as if determined not to lose. Jung Heewon whistled.
“Looking good, Sangah-ssi!”

Dionysus had already finished his tenth toast in a corner. I also saw Cheok Jungyeong sharing drinks with the ‘Hasty Swamp Judge.’ Though it was a small banquet, the sight put me more at ease than any banquet I had attended before.
[A rare moment of rest. Congratulations, Demon King of Salvation.]
I turned to find an old man standing there in an elegant suit.
“You’ve arrived, Mass Production Maker.”
He, too, was one of the constellations who had helped in this ‘selection.’
[I enjoyed your Story. You certainly had reason to talk big at the Gourmet Association.]
“You flatter me.”
I picked up a glass from the table and clinked glasses with the ‘Mass Production Maker.’
The smell told me it was quite strong, so I merely touched it to my lips and set it back down.
Neither of us spoke for a moment.
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ was probably choosing his question.
And that question was precisely why he and the other constellations were here—and why I had held this banquet.
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ took a sip and spoke as if in passing.
[Now that you’ve obtained the ‘Qualification for the End,’ I suppose the filtering has been lifted.]
I felt a subtle change in the atmosphere.
I nodded and replied,
“It has.”

The hall was still boisterous, but one by one, the constellations’ eyes turned toward me. Persephone, Cheok Jungyeong, Dionysus…… In truth, they had all been listening to our conversation while pretending to be uninterested.
Once every constellation’s gaze was fixed on me, the ‘Mass Production Maker’ asked,
[May I ask what your ■■ was?]
What was my ■■?
I had naturally expected that question from the ‘Mass Production Maker.’
“Are you curious?”
[Is there anyone here who isn’t?]

As the Mass Production Maker smiled faintly, several constellations cleared their throats. Sensing the unusual turn in the atmosphere, my other companions, who still didn’t understand what was happening, began to focus on me too.
“Why is everyone suddenly……”
“Shh.”
Jung Heewon stopped Lee Hyunsung from cluelessly interrupting.
I slowly looked around at everyone present. Before I knew it, every being in the hall was watching me.
In ‘Ways of Survival,’ it went by a great many names.
For example, the ‘King of the Dokkaebis’ had said this:
「The end and beginning of every story.」
But Yoo Joonghyuk would say this:
「The goddamn Star Stream.」

Lee Hyunsung would call it “discharge from the military,” and Yoo Sangah might call it “retirement planning.” For Lee Jihye, it would be “graduation.” And surprisingly, none of those interpretations of ■■ would be wrong.
The Mass Production Maker asked,
[Everyone who obtains the ‘Qualification for the End’ receives a different name for their ‘end.’ Did you know that?]
“Since everyone possesses different Stories, I suppose that’s only natural.”

■■ had never been a proper noun whose exact meaning could be communicated. The filtering being lifted simply meant I could now ‘read’ it. The other constellations who had received a hidden scenario like mine were probably all in a similar position.
<Hidden Scenario ― A Single Story>
Category: Hidden
Difficulty: ???
Clear Conditions: Complete a single Story that will reach ■■.
Time Limit: ―
Reward: ???
Failure: ???
●At present, you have completed ‘Beginning (起).’
●For details, refer to the additional scenario description.
The hidden scenario, ‘A Single Story.’
This scenario was assigned to every being who obtained the ‘Qualification for the End.’
To search a sea of countless Stories in the vast galaxy of the <Star Stream> and complete a single ‘perfect story.’
Legendary-grade Stories, Myth-grade Stories, and even the Giant Story I had obtained were ultimately only steps on the journey toward that ‘single story.’
The Mass Production Maker in front of me and Persephone over there would have received this scenario too. Of course, the places they ultimately reached would be different from mine.
[Baat!]
Before I could even tell her, Biyoo cut off the channel in the hall.
She had probably sensed instinctively that what we were about to discuss was important.
As protesting messages from constellations flowed out of the air, the ‘Mass Production Maker’ spoke in a solemn tone.
[My ■■ was ‘Exhaustion (枯渴).’]
I was a little surprised, not having expected him to reveal his hand so readily.
Then Persephone, who had been dancing on the stage, spoke as well.
[Mine was ‘Death.’]
Exhaustion and Death.
Both were words that could symbolize the ‘end’ of something.
They were also deeply paradoxical ends for the ‘Mass Production Maker,’ who always loved to make things, and ‘Persephone,’ who ruled the Underworld of the dead.
Now that they had shown their cards, I had nowhere left to retreat.
“Everyone, please swear on your modifiers that you won’t reveal what you hear from me here to anyone.”
Several constellations looked at one another at my words.
[Well, of course……]
[Ahem, is that really necessary? As if we’d go around telling anyone……]
[Just how extraordinary is your ■■ for you to keep us in such suspense?]
I didn’t answer immediately. I merely smiled.
A quiet ripple began to spread among the constellations.
[Could it be……?]
It felt as though I could see the thoughts flashing through their minds.
Watching their expressions, I thought,
Yes, think.
Ponder it. Question it.
Only then would the outcome I wanted take shape.
At last, when the constellations’ murmuring reached its peak, I slowly began to speak.
Han Sooyoung was walking down a street.
The landscape of Seoul lay in ruins. She was walking alone through streets without a single survivor.
All kinds of wild thoughts flitted through her mind.
Why am I here right now?
I was definitely fighting the constellations with Flame Dragon.
No, more importantly, ‘Seoul’ was supposed to be sealed off, so why……
―Flame Dragon?
The ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ didn’t answer.
―Hey, is anyone there?

Han Sooyoung shouted as she walked among collapsed multi-tenant buildings. Monster corpses lay strewn among the familiar ruined buildings of Gwanghwamun. Every time she passed one of the reeking corpses, goosebumps rose on her skin.
Every single one was a monster far beyond her current ability to handle.
What the hell. What happened?
She could ask, but there was no one to answer.
No, even if there were, perhaps it would be better if they didn’t answer.
If any ‘being’ remained alive here, it would be the terrifying monster that had reduced all those creatures to bloody pulp.
If this was a dream, she could only pray to wake up……
That was when something like a person’s shadow flashed past in the distance.
A familiar human figure (人形) in a white, pure-white coat.
Her heart swelled.
―Kim Dokja!
The moment the man turned toward her.
With the sound of flesh being pierced, a blade suddenly burst through his coat.
The white coat staining red.
Han Sooyoung woke with a scream.
“Hah, hah……”
Only after she blinked several times did her sense of reality slowly return.
“What the……”
Uncharacteristically, she even spoke to herself.
Her back was drenched in cold sweat.
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ is pleased that you are talking to yourself.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon,’ that you have finally become his true successor……]
“Shut up.”
With the Black Flame Dragon spouting nonsense, this certainly seemed to be reality.
Han Sooyoung pressed one hand to her temple.
……Why had he appeared in her dream?

Normally, Han Sooyoung would have dismissed it as a meaningless dream. But in a world where superstitions became reality, she couldn’t simply brush off even a dream like this. A moment later, she realized that the arm she had raised to her temple was wrapped in bandages.
“Goddammit. I still haven’t taken these off.”
“Leave them on. They’re there because you’re hurt.”
Startled, she turned to find a woman she knew standing there.
“……Kim Dokja’s mom?”
“You’re the only one who still calls me that.”
Lee Sookyung wiped Han Sooyoung’s back and forehead with a towel.
Han Sooyoung asked,
“Why didn’t you go to the Demon Realm?”
“How could I show my face there?”
“Kim Dokja would’ve liked it.”
“He would have liked it more if you’d gone.”
“……You don’t know your own son very well, ajumma.”

Han Sooyoung spoke with a slight pout. Lee Sookyung smiled faintly and replaced the damp pillowcase with a fresh one. Apparently liking the new pillowcase, Han Sooyoung buried her nose in it and sniffed before speaking.
“Still, it looks like things worked out somehow.”

Rrrrrumble!

Whiiiiine……
Star Relics rising into the air, shedding brilliant light. They were all ‘keys’ that would be used to clear this scenario.

Yoo Joonghyuk, looking at me with empty eyes.

An eternal sleep without dreams, from which he could not be awakened.

“You decided to seal Yoo Joonghyuk in this round forever.”

To survive once more and reach the next scenario.

Rrrrrumble!
Powerful currents of energy began to flow from Han Sooyoung’s body.

That to surpass the original, she had to break free of it.

Tzzzzzt……

“Don’t tell me you’re……”

“It’s no use, Kim Dokja! That method……!”

“Gabriel, Jophiel! Please help me!”
[The constellation ‘Lily Blooming in Aquarius’ looks at you.]
[The constellation ‘Commander of the Red Cosmos’ looks at you.]

If I could sever this link, even for a moment, I might be able to save Yoo Joonghyuk.
“Yoo Joonghyuk, hold yourself together!”
Yoo Joonghyuk now possessed enough Stories to become a ‘constellation.’

Rooooooar!
The Demon King’s Status and the archangel’s Status I had unleashed flowed into the Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword at the same time.
My opponent was Yoo Joonghyuk’s unidentified constellation.
Severing that link would require at least this much power.
I brought the Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword down.
Claaaaaang!
Once more.
Claaaang!
And once more.

The [Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword] in my hand snapped in two.
I stared at Yoo Joonghyuk’s link. It didn’t have so much as a scratch.
[The constellation ‘Lily Blooming in Aquarius’ feels an inexplicable terror.]
[The constellation ‘Commander of the Red Cosmos’ is aghast.]
For a moment, I felt as if the distant cosmos were looking at me.
It was a will whose origins I could not guess, so immense I could not even begin to fathom it.
[The sponsor of the incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ looks at you.]
Seized by intense vertigo, for an instant I felt as though the entire history of my life were warping.
Yoo Joonghyuk’s sponsor. I couldn’t tell exactly what it was. I could neither describe nor explain it. All I could grasp was this
Immensely powerful and pure.
Something like desire in its primal form had been there.
Something like a baby’s laughter echoed in my ears. When I came to my senses again, the broken halves of the Four Tiger Evil Cutting Sword lay on the ground.

Han Sooyoung, wearing a strange smile.

Perhaps Han Sooyoung had seen the sponsor’s true nature more clearly than I had.

I did not answer. Han Sooyoung continued.

[The exclusive skill ‘Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint’ activates!]
[Your understanding of this individual is sufficient. ‘Stage 2’ of Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint activates!]
Then I could hear what was inside Yoo Joonghyuk’s mind. His consciousness had sunk so deep that most of the words drifted through the air like dust.

「I want to die.」
「I want to die.」
What I was seeing now was a human being’s inner life, suppressed within the text of ‘Ways of Survival.’

It was a very small voice. A very faint voice among the countless voices pouring down.

“……Still being stubborn?”
I looked at Yoo Joonghyuk.
I had definitely heard it.
I could still hear it.
「I want to live.」
That one voice, so faint, so very faint.

I gripped ‘Unbreakable Faith.’

The Holy Sword Ascalon.
The Thunder Sword Gram.
The Dragon-Cleaving Sword Ridill.
The Dragon-Slaying Sword Arondight.
Swords bearing Stories of dragon slaying.

“You crazy bastard……!”

“I won’t return to the 3rd round.”

“I’ll make it myself.”

Whiiiiiine!

Crrrrrack!

[Avatar].

Jophiel’s 503rd Legion was the perfect answer to copies moving in all directions like that.

[The constellation ‘Lily Blooming in Aquarius’ bestows her blessing upon you.]

[The constellation ‘Commander of the Red Cosmos’ is flustered.]

[The five keys connect with the sealing sphere.]
Han Sooyoung shouted.

[The scenario’s clear conditions have been fulfilled.]

[All constellations of the nebula ‘Vedas’ gasp in horror.]
[All constellations of the nebula ‘Papyrus’ grow wary.]

「Hee hee」

Grrrrrrrr……

The chief culprit behind <Eden>’s destruction, and the worst calamity in the <Star Stream>.

Had been able to live.

“Damn it……!”

[Follow me. The Scribe is waiting.]
“······How long do I have to wait?”

Jung Heewon and I had been led straight to <Eden>'s palace. <Eden> was far more modest than I had imagined. I was familiar with it from the descriptions in ‘Ways of Survival,’ but it was certainly different from the other great nebulae.
Simple decorations without any particular air of pretension. There was an almost strange humility to the ceiling and the statues in the wall niches, all rendered in plain white.
The problem was that this humility was making my wait even more tedious.
―Wait here. Someone will come to guide you soon.
Uriel had said she would show Jung Heewon around the palace, then disappeared somewhere, leaving me here.
I wanted to look around <Eden>, too······ I felt a little hurt.
······It was probably because of what had happened in the 1863rd round.
After all, I had left her companion Jophiel there.
Even if she resented me, there was nothing I could do about it.
[Kim Dokja, u made it?]

I looked up blankly to find an angel seated on a cloud, looking down at me. A figure who looked to be in their early teens, with curly hair. Seeing the angel gazing down at me with a half-asleep look, I sprang to my feet.

Raphael nodded.
Raphael, the Guardian of Youths and Travel.
This trip to <Eden> seemed to be a lucky one. To think I would see Raphael's true body after Uriel's. Still······ Was this archangel really the one who had repelled that terrifying ‘Asmodeus’?
[How'd u find out about the ‘secret portal’?]
“Jophiel told me.”
[How do u feel about being in <Eden>?]
“It's wonderful.”
[······You look sleepy, though?]
I hurriedly composed myself and smiled. Raphael led me into a passage off the reception room, as if telling me to follow.
As we walked along the outer corridor, the garden came into view through the open windows. Sheep grazing here and there looked up at me and bleated softly. Looking at them, I asked,
“So <Eden> really does have ‘lambs.’”
[Nod. Good for counting when u can't sleep.]
“······Are they out there so we can count them?”
[U've probably seen them too. When u close ur eyes before bed and picture sheep, they're the ones that show up.]
I was astonished. This was something that didn't even appear in ‘Ways of Survival.’
Those were really the sheep people counted before bed?
[Was lying.]
I stared at Raphael, dumbfounded. He grinned and began speaking again.
[Did u know? <Eden> didn't have any sheep originally.]
“······Are you lying again?”
[This one's true. Uriel brought the sheep here.]
······Uriel? Why?
[Scribe gave Uriel a sub-scenario once.]

The archangels of <Eden> received their missions through the ‘Scribe of Heaven.’ And naturally, every mission in the <Star Stream> came down to a ‘scenario.’ This, too, was a story absent from ‘Ways of Survival,’ so it piqued my curiosity.
“What was the scenario?”
[‘Bring back ten lambs.’]
Many of the <Star Stream>'s scenarios were framed in ‘figurative language.’ And in <Eden>, ‘lambs’ was an unmistakable metaphor. Put simply, Metatron had wanted Uriel to bring back ten believers.
“······Don't tell me Uriel brought back ‘actual sheep’?”
[Nod. Started with ten. They bred, so now there's that many.]
······Somehow, that seemed very like Uriel.
Here and there, I could also see angels tending the sheep. Angels shearing their wool or feeding them. They were all beautiful, just as ‘Ways of Survival’ had described.

A few of them looked over and began whispering among themselves. One, two, three······ Their numbers steadily grew. Someone fashioned a banner on the spot out of the shorn wool and began waving it at me.
······What did it say?
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ puts on a stern expression.]
Pale with fright, the angels hurriedly scattered. In the distance, I could see Uriel and Jung Heewon waving at me. Raphael clicked his tongue and added,
[Angels, honestly······ They just love fallen humans.]
“So you can speak normally?”
[Head on in. Scribe's waiting for u.]
Before I knew it, the Scribe's office was right in front of me.
I drew a gentle, deep breath, then opened the door and went inside.
The first thing that met my eyes was a feast of books piled as high as a person.

There were so many books that a lifetime of reading wouldn't seem enough to get through them. I found myself warming to the room's owner without even realizing it. There were no bad people among book lovers, after all.
I stepped farther into the office, taking care not to knock over the books. Beyond the mountains of books, I could see a desk. And seated at it was an ash-haired archangel with a tired face.
[You have arrived.]
His voice held a solemnity unlike that of any constellation I had encountered. Metatron pushed up his glasses and smiled at me.
[It is a pleasure to meet you, ‘Demon King of Salvation.’ I am the ‘Scribe of Heaven.’]
I had come to <Eden> for two main reasons.
One was my ostensible purpose, and the other was my real one.
[First, I would like to hear what happened in the other worldline.]
I nodded and began my account.
From making a contract with the ‘Secretive Plotter’ and traveling to the worldline of the 1863rd round, to meeting the people there and returning here with Jophiel left behind.

I finished my account, speaking honestly of some things, briefly of others, and leaving certain things unspoken. Metatron listened attentively. He listened seriously to some things, calmly to others. And some seemed to interest him.
[The ‘Secretive Plotter’······.]
“······Do you know them?”
Metatron smiled faintly.
[There is probably no constellation in this world that has not heard of that being. But there is probably no constellation that knows who they are, either.]
I soon fell silent. That was the end of my account.
[Thank you for telling me your story, Demon King of Salvation.]
“Not at all.”
[So <Eden> will fall in the future, after all.]
For someone speaking of ruin, his voice was utterly calm. His face showed not the slightest disturbance. I quietly watched him, then asked,
“Why did you summon me? Surely it wasn't simply to hear my story.”
The Scribe of Heaven.
The one who recorded everything in <Eden>, and <Eden>'s second-in-command.
Metatron's smile deepened.
[Why do you think I summoned you?]
This was how Metatron conducted a conversation.
Hearing his own desires from the other person's lips.
I thought for a moment, then answered.
Perhaps this was an opportunity for me.
“You must be planning to use me as a tool to prevent ‘ruin.’”
[You? What use would you be?]
My reflection shone in Metatron's clear eyes.
The Kim Dokja in one eye had white wings, while the Kim Dokja in the other spread the black wings of a Demon King.
“Because I'm a ‘Demon King’ who hasn't chosen an alliance.”
Through the previous ‘Demon King Selection,’ I had become the Demon Realm's ‘73rd Demon King.’
A seat that had stood vacant for thousands of years.
And I, a newborn constellation, had taken that seat.
I opened my old message logs.
[The Demon King ‘Black Mane Lion’ invited you to their demon realm.]
[The Demon King ‘Immeasurable Austerity’ invited you to their demon realm.]
These were messages from the demon realms that had accumulated from the moment I became a Demon King until now
“<Eden>'s ruin is set in motion by a war with the <Demon Realm>. You must be planning to use me as a mediator.”
Since I had risen to the rank of Demon King, it was only natural that I would attract the attention of the other demon realms.
Then what about <Eden>?
<Eden>, too, had shown an unusual interest in me since before I became a Demon King.
Beginning with Uriel, and extending to the goodwill shown by the other archangels.
Considering <Eden>'s past attitude toward evil-aligned constellations, its treatment of me was so unusual it could almost be called a break with convention.
“You need me. In the history of the <Star Stream>, I'm probably the first being to attract the interest of both the Demon Realm and Eden at the same time.”
I deliberately raised my voice.
With the negotiations ahead in mind, letting Metatron intimidate me here would do me no good.
Without answering, Metatron quietly studied my face for a moment.
And the next moment, I realized something was wrong.
A dazzling light was rising behind Metatron, accompanied by an overwhelming sense of pressure.
I sensed a fanatical gaze from somewhere. I could feel a dangerous power relentlessly probing my very existence.
[The exclusive skill ‘Fourth Wall’ activates powerfully!]
Tzzzzzt!
Sparks obscured my vision, and I groaned as I took several steps back.
Through the gradually subsiding sparks, Metatron spoke in an admiring voice.
[······So it was you after all. The one chosen by a ‘fragment of the Final Wall.’]
[The ‘Wall that Divides Good and Evil’ looks at you in surprise.]
Startled, I looked ahead.
A silver ‘wall’ rippling behind Metatron.
There was no mistaking it.
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ bares its teeth at the ‘Wall that Divides Good and Evil.’]
The Wall that Divides Good and Evil.
The archangel Metatron, too, was the owner of a ‘wall,’ just like me.
Taste of Ruin
「What a stub born fellow」
It seemed the [Fourth Wall] knew that wall.
It had received a brief mention in ‘Ways of Survival,’ too. One of the walls that, like Jang Hayoung’s ‘Unidentifiable Wall,’ possessed great power but had unknown origins.
[The ‘Wall that Divides Good and Evil’ weighs your good and evil.]
[The ‘Fourth Wall’ snorts.]

A power that distinguished good and evil within the <Star Stream> in response to Metatron’s reasonable suspicions. But one thing was certain: he intended to use me to prepare for <Eden>’s coming destruction.
[The wall upon which the ■■ of all these worlds is written. You must have read of <Eden>’s destruction there. Is that not so?]
I was a little surprised. The Metatron of this round seemed somewhat different from the one I knew.

“Do you know what this ‘Final Wall’ is?”
Metatron’s expression became inscrutable at my question.
[Are you asking out of genuine curiosity, or do you have some other purpose?]
Instead of answering, I quietly stared into Metatron’s eyes.
Metatron smiled wryly.
[······Very well. In return, please turn off the channel now. I imagine everyone has seen enough of <Eden> by now.]
Indirect messages erupted in the air at those words.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ scratches his head vigorously.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ throws a fit, biting his nails.]
[The constellation ‘Bald General of Justice’ is moved by the sights of heaven.]
[Some constellations are satisfied with their tour of Eden!]
[You have received 50,000 coins in sponsorship.]
As with the <Underworld>, quite a few constellations must have been curious about <Eden>. I heard a “Baat” along with the sound of Biyoo closing the channel.
Stroking the bindings of the piled-up books, Metatron began his story.
[The ‘Final Wall’ constitutes the very essence of this world. It had existed for a very long time, crumbling little by little, before it finally collapsed.]

“How many people have ‘walls’ like these?”

[No one knows which Story will be chosen in the end.]

Metatron turned toward his office window. The sunlight falling into <Eden> illuminated his handsome face, leaving some parts in deep shadow and others unnaturally bright. For a moment, the unfair light made his face appear strangely distorted.

Star Relic Fruit and Star Relic Liquid······.

“······Then there’s no way.”
I felt a little disheartened.
I’d hoped <Eden> might be able to do something, but apparently even that was impossible. Then Metatron added something.

The office door creaked open. A man walking into the office, knocking down the high stacks of books. At the sight of his incarnation body, cloaked in dazzling radiance, I instinctively activated my Status throughout my body.

Jung Heewon toured <Eden> feeling almost as if she were on a picnic. Most of the angels were friendly, and some asked her questions. Most were about Kim Dokja or Yoo Joonghyuk, but she thought that was only natural. Those two were currently the most closely watched beings on the Korean Peninsula.

[Yes, Heewon.]

When she turned, Uriel was also staring that way with a stiff expression.

Uriel nodded.
A sound like a massive train derailing filled my ears.
Ruuuumble!
Merely facing him seemed to bring a flood of memories back.
This was <Eden>, and that constellation wouldn’t attack me here. Even so, my ‘Status’ reacted this violently. It had to be an instinct born of memory.

Four arms attached to the man’s torso.

Soma, the Star Relic Liquid of <Vedas>.

A share in the Giant Story, <Gigantomachia>.

[The ‘Fourth Wall’ nods.]
[The ‘Wall that Divides Good and Evil’ watches its owner closely.]

「Kim Dokja recalled the 1863rd round.」
I wouldn’t lose anyone anymore.
「Information from ‘Ways of Survival’ surfaced and vanished in Kim Dokja’s mind.」
The battles ahead might draw in constellations of the highest order.
Not only Surya, but other high gods of <Vedas>—the <Lokapala>—might make a move. Some of <Olympus>’ twelve chief gods would also join the scenario.

······Michael, huh.
「At last, Kim Dokja made his decision.」

Gabriel’s indirect message, heard from somewhere.

A noisy street reminiscent of a battlefield. On the way to the auction house, countless street vendors sold every kind of item.

An unfathomable Story of darkness unfurling in the air.

Athena, the ‘Spokesman of Justice and Wisdom’; Apollo, the ‘Almighty Sun’; Hermes, the ‘Master of the Skywalk’; Dionysus, the ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy.’ And Briareus, the hundred-handed giant, too.

The king of the Underworld and the king of the sea.

Beings whose Status could shake the world with nothing more than an exchange of glances.

A voice as cold as the deep sea.

But Theseus’ true body would also have taken enough damage to leave him unable to participate in scenarios for a while.
Taking all of that into account, Theseus had thrown himself forward to complete this scenario.
[All ‘leaders’ on <Olympus>’ side have died!]
[The scenario’s clear conditions have been met!]
[Calculating the contributions of individual incarnations and constellations!]
[‘First-Person Protagonist’s Viewpoint’ has ended.]
Blood gushed from my mouth as I returned to my body.
Inside the ruined Pluto.
Kim Namwoon’s voice reached me.
[Don’t summon me anymore······ Grasshopper Man. Bye······.]
Its summoning time over, Pluto was returning to the <Underworld>.
At the same time, an enormous underwater storm raged through the area where Theseus’ incarnation body had vanished.
Ruuuuuumble!
Poseidon, who had descended into Theseus’ incarnation body, was running wild.
Incarnations writhed amid the raging spray, struggling to breathe.
Some of the Status pouring from Poseidon surged toward the defenseless Yoo Joonghyuk.
Already badly wounded and left in tatters after drawing upon the 362nd round’s talent, Yoo Joonghyuk couldn’t evade the attack.
I shouted,
[Hades!]
[Understood.]
Hades appeared out of thin air with ‘Kynee’ and pulled Yoo Joonghyuk into his arms.
Poseidon’s spear merely shattered the innocent deep-sea floor.
But the danger wasn’t over.
A fissure was rapidly widening around Triaina, which had struck the seabed.
Whoooooosh!
The fissure soon began sucking in everything around it like a vacuum cleaner.

Unfortunately, I was among the things being cleaned up. My gravely injured incarnation body had no strength to resist the suction. My hand, reaching out into emptiness as I was swept along by the current.
But there was no one to take my hand.
······Or so I thought.
「Dokja-ssi!」
「You idiot!」

Hair spread beautifully through the water. Swimming over like a mermaid, Lee Seolhwa took my left arm, and Han Sooyoung, who had come with her, grabbed my right. After pressing the pressure points around my wounds, the two pulled me upward with all their strength.
I could see Han Sooyoung’s profile as she swam desperately, trying to get even a little farther from the deep-sea fissure.
Before long, we safely broke the surface.
“Pwah!”
“Kim Dokja, you lunatic!”
[The main scenario will end soon!]
Instead of answering Han Sooyoung, I studied the currents.
If I was right, having lost the incarnation body he’d descended into, Poseidon would now have no choice but to return.
[The constellation ‘Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea’ roars!]
But events unfolded differently from my expectations.
Tzzzzzzzzzt!
Poseidon’s power, which should have weakened, was growing stronger.
The companions seemed to sense something was wrong, too.
[The <Bureau> advises the ‘Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea’ to withdraw!]
Despite the <Bureau>’s recommendation, Poseidon’s Status wasn’t fading.
The situation was clear.
An unjustified rampage in a scenario already finished.
[The <Bureau> prepares sanctions against the ‘Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea.’]
Fortunately, the <Bureau> seemed to be doing its job properly, too.
I examined the signs of Status bubbling up beneath the sea.
The problem was what Poseidon would do before the sanctions took effect······.
A little way off, Hades and Persephone were watching us.
[Many constellations condemn the ‘Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea’!]
[Shut—up!]
A wave of True Voice (眞言派) that seemed to bleach my mind white.
In the distance, a tsunami-like wave was approaching.
It was hundreds of meters high.
“Fuck! What’s that!”
“Poseidon’s gone mad!”
The incarnations who belatedly came to their senses tried to flee, but it was already too late.
Some, including giants, were swept up in the first wave.
The immense Status of the sea that no one could resist.
I looked at Hades, but he wasn’t stepping forward.
The reason was obvious.
Hades was thinking exactly the same thing I was.
Like a father and son (父子) counting stars, we looked up at the sky together.
「However little interest you have in <Olympus>, you won’t be able to just watch this time.」
[The <Bureau> grants probability to someone.]
The next moment, the sky changed color.
A light that paralyzed even sight and hearing flashed across the sky that had been blue moments before.
It was a light that seemed to erase the world.
Only a little later did I realize it had been an enormous thunderbolt.
A thunderbolt tearing the waves apart.
Lightning powerful enough to split the sea in two and scorch even the ground deep beneath it black.
Poseidon’s final roar rang out like a death cry.
Gaaaaaah······!
[The constellation ‘Spear that Parts the Boundaries of the Sea’ has exited the scenario.]
It was an unbelievable sight.
Yet it had really happened.
[The constellation ‘Lightning Throne’ looks down upon <Olympus>.]
A Status none of the twelve divine seats could dare face.
The moment the indirect message appeared, every god of <Olympus> froze.
Even the insolent Dionysus. Even the noble Athena and Artemis.
The sky’s gaze slowly shifted, this time toward the king of the Underworld.
「The world below and the sky faced each other.」
As though that was conversation enough, Hades, wearing ‘Kynee,’ vanished from the scenario.
[The constellation ‘Father of the Rich Night’ has exited the scenario.]
Persephone disappeared with him, winking at me.
[We’ll meet again soon, our dear little son.]
Two of the three chief gods had vanished in an instant, but the tension didn’t diminish at all.
With the sound of the world’s scales moving, the balance of probability tilted once more.
Now it was clear whom the <Bureau> had granted probability to.
Zeus, king of Olympus.
The only being in the great nebula <Olympus> to reach the ‘Final Scenario.’
No constellation could have been better suited than Zeus to expelling Poseidon and drawing reactions from the others.
Indeed, Biyoo’s channel felt almost like a festival.
[The <Bureau>’s Great Dokkaebis reclaim the probability granted to the ‘Lightning Throne.’]
[The <Bureau>’s Great Dokkaebis advise the ‘Lightning Throne’ to withdraw!]
But a festival was a ‘festival’ because it was brief.

If a being of Zeus’ caliber remained long in a lower scenario, it would disrupt the <Star Stream>’s balance. A misstep could even bring a catastrophe like ‘The Indescribable Distance,’ as had happened before.
But Zeus, true to himself, was utterly arrogant.
[Do not rush me. I did not come at the request of the likes of you. I came to see my seeds.]
With those words, <Olympus>’ sky looked down upon the twelve divine seats.
Even the twelve divine seats, who looked down upon the world, were tense before Zeus’ gaze.
[And still······ nothing but trash.]
At a single remark from Zeus, the twelve divine seats sank down as though dealt a heavy blow.
I saw Dionysus’ shoulders trembling. As a ‘Narrative-grade constellation,’ he should have been able to resist at least a little, yet he couldn’t resist at all.
Some ‘stories’ were like that.
Built up and accumulated for so long that, in the end, resistance became impossible.
The clouds cleared, and Zeus’ Status grew faint.
Like a farmer turning his back on barren soil, Zeus was leaving the scenario.
One of the twelve divine seats murmured,
[We weren’t even children to him······?]
And at that very moment.
Whoosh!
A small stone flew toward the sky.
I had thrown it.
Tzzzzzzzzzt!
Struck by sparks of probability, the stone vanished in midair.
[The constellation ‘Lightning Throne’ glares at you.]
For a moment, I felt a powerful ‘Status’ constrict my whole body, but I only glared all the more fiercely at the sky.
That was all the probability Zeus was permitted anyway.
[The constellation ‘Lightning Throne’ exits the scenario.]
Turning to the twelve divine seats, I spoke.
“Why do you just sit there and listen to that?”
[······What on earth are you—]
Just as Dionysus, seemingly incredulous, was about to speak, messages poured from the sky.
No, they weren’t messages.
Dionysus, who had been about to say something, the twelve divine seats, and I, too. We all looked up at the sky Zeus had left.
Snow as white as stars was falling.
Snow unrelated to Zeus, ruler of the sky.
Perhaps the power of a constellation who had existed long before Zeus.
It was the light of the being who had ruled the first sky, before <Olympus> was even created.
Standing in the sea like lonely islands, Briareus and the Gigantes howled at the falling snow.
[Main Scenario #60 — ‘Gigantomachia’ has ended.]
[Hidden Scenario — ‘Myth Subversion’ has been completed.]
[Reward calculation begins.]
The world’s constellations were watching me. Beyond the four main constellations, there were others I already knew, and others I barely knew.
Dionysus spoke.
[······You won, Kim Dokja.]
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and the giants floated their huge bodies like boats and carried us.

Yoo Joonghyuk and Han Sooyoung each looked toward a different part of the sky, their thoughts unknown. Jung Heewon and Lee Hyunsung supported each other, while Lee Seolhwa clasped her own hands tightly. Holding Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung, Lee Jihye wiped away tears.
Perhaps they, too, were hearing their own system messages.
[You have obtained a new ‘Giant Story’!]
[You have additionally obtained three new Stories!]
It was a plan I’d spent a very long time preparing.
And so, as though reading a novel with an ending already fixed, I could see clearly what would happen next.
[Your second Giant Story has completed ‘Development (承)’!]
[The second condition of Hidden Scenario — ‘A Single Story’ has been fulfilled!]
At last, the ‘Development (承)’ I’d awaited would greet me.
[The nebula <Kim Dokja’s Company>’s renown spreads throughout the <Star Stream>.]
System messages celebrating our victory would resound throughout the universe.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ raises Ruyi Jingu Bang!]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ waves his bandages of liberation!]
[The constellation ‘Secretive Plotter’ nods.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is proud of you.]
The four in my channel would congratulate me, too.
[Some constellations of the ‘Final Scenario’ take notice of you.]
And beings of the ‘Final Scenario,’ like Zeus, would begin to notice me.
[The Demon Realm’s Demon Kings watch your movements closely.]
[<Eden>’s archangels take notice of you.]
[Unknown Outer Gods gaze at your existence.]
[The ‘Seekers of the End’ listen to your story.]
In the middle of a sea dusted with white snow, good and evil, and beings belonging to neither side, would watch the story.
The end of a myth that had ruled this world for ages.
And the people who had created that story with me would look for me.
“Kim Dokja.”
But by then.
“······Kim Dokja?”
I would already be gone.

title: A Road That Isn’t a Road

paragraphs.text: A Road That Isn’t a Road
Immediately after <Olympus>'s <Gigantomachia> collapsed, the restrictions binding the giants vanished. Freed from their ancient Story, they would now become participants in new scenarios.
[I have no wish to repeat our predecessors' battle. Do you agree?]
[I agree.]
And so, with the end of Scenario 60 just ahead, Briareus, leader of the giants, and Dionysus, temporary representative of the 12 Seats, reached a dramatic agreement.
[<Star Stream> acknowledges the ‘collapse of the myth’.]
[A new Story blooms in Scenario 60.]
In truth, they might have been able to keep fighting if they wanted to.

But <Gigantomachia> had drastically weakened <Olympus>'s fighting strength. Many heroes and giants had died, the whereabouts of ‘Poseidon’ were unknown, and the silent ‘King of the Underworld’ had announced his successor.
If the remaining 12 Seats and the giants continued their confrontation now, they would only endanger the nebula's existence.
The fall of the great nebula <Olympus>.
At the center of that incredible story was one small nebula.
[Many constellations chant the name ‘Kim Dokja's Company’!]
That story, which had begun with one small constellation's struggle, was at last bringing a ‘Giant Story’ to its close.
Yet the members of that nebula had no time to savor the lingering emotion of the ending of the ‘Giant Story’. They were calling someone's name.
“Dokja-ssi! Dokja-ssi!”
“Hyung! Stop playing around! Where are you hiding?”
Jung Heewon, Lee Hyunsung, Lee Jihye, Shin Yoosung, Lee Gilyoung······.
They were searching for Kim Dokja on a small island the giants had made.
Some with anxious voices, others with disbelieving faces.
Amid the confusion, the only one who remained calm was a man gazing up at the sky without expression.
Han Sooyoung glared intently at him, then asked:
“Yoo Joonghyuk. You know something, don't you?”
“Answer me. The kids are worried.”
Yoo Joonghyuk slowly turned toward Han Sooyoung.
Noticing something, the others gathered behind her.
“What is it, Master? Do you know something?”
“Nothing's happened to Dokja-ssi again, has it?”
After a short silence, Yoo Joonghyuk answered.
“Kim Dokja will have returned to Earth.”
“What? Without us?”
Realization belatedly dawned on Lee Jihye, and her mouth fell slightly open.
“Ah······Could it be?”

Come to think of it, <Gigantomachia> hadn't been their real objective. Participating in it had been only a step along the way. While everyone else was intoxicated with victory, Kim Dokja alone had been thinking about the real purpose of all this.
Jung Heewon let out a sigh of relief and said with a wry smile:
“······Even so, I'll have a few things to say about him running straight home by himself.”
“Let's hurry back, too!”
Just then, a system message appeared.
[Leaving the area is restricted for 1 hour to stabilize the scenario.]
Lee Seolhwa asked, her eyes wide with surprise.
“······How on earth did Dokja-ssi get out?”
“He probably used some special method.”
“A special method?”
“I don't know the details, either.”
With that answer, Yoo Joonghyuk looked up at the sky again.
Snow was still falling. Snow fluttering through brilliant summer weather. On Earth, it would have been like snow falling in August.
Watching it, Han Sooyoung asked Yoo Joonghyuk:
“······Kim Dokja went back first because of Yoo Sangah, didn't he?”
There was always a reason to ask the obvious.
Yoo Joonghyuk answered only after the miraculous flurry had melted away in the sunlight.
“We'll find out when we get there.”
Inside the car racing along a dimensional road (次元路), I briefly lost myself in thought.
When I first began planning to overturn <Gigantomachia>, I contacted several constellations. Probably every constellation who was even slightly acquainted with me received a message.
Most had special ties to <Olympus> or circumstances that made joining Scenario 60 difficult. I understood. What constellation would want to make an enemy of a great nebula like <Olympus>?
But one of them made an unusual offer.
―I cannot help you with <Gigantomachia>. But I can open an escape route if you fail. For you alone, however.
And the one who had made that offer now sat at ease in the driver's seat, holding the wheel.
[······I never imagined you'd use my offer like this.]
A being who could pass through a ‘scenario’ portal with his own probability, and the owner of a [Special Ferrarghini] that could travel dimensional roads at will.
‘Mass Production Maker’ smiled as he spoke.
[You used to be the sort who rarely asked anyone for help.]
“My thinking changed a little after I visited another worldline.”
I smiled and added:
“Besides, I accidentally left my [X-grade Ferrarghini] behind. I haven't even finished paying the installments. I still tear up whenever I think about it.”
[Hahaha. You mean the car you bought from me?]
“So I've decided to stop driving my own car and get rides in other people's cars from now on.”
[Oh dear. As the seller, I find that a regrettable decision. A new model just came out, and I was going to give you one for free.]
“······For free?”
[I'm lying.]
······I knew it. That sly old constellation would never willingly take a loss.

With a thick cigar between his lips, ‘Mass Production Maker’ seemed to consider something for a moment. The drifting smoke was sucked into a vent in front of the glove compartment before it could reach me in the passenger seat.
[I'd like to make a ‘contract’ with your nebula.]
“A contract?”
[Do you realize what you've done this time?]
I knew.
How could I not?
[The Giant Story ‘Torch That Swallowed the Myth’ flows through your Story veins (說脈)!]
Even now, the ‘result’ of what I'd done was flowing through every vein in my body.
「Torch That Swallowed the Myth」.

It wasn't 「One Who Erases God's Fingerprints」 or 「One Who Closes the Gate of Myth」, the Stories I'd originally wanted. But its essence was similar. A Story earned by fighting a great nebula and overturning a myth. It would serve as a counter to the countless nebulas I would fight in the future.
[What happened has made many constellations aware of <Kim Dokja's Company>.]
“I imagine so.”
[Some even insist that your nebula should be counted among the <Twelve Great Nebulas>.]
······The Twelve Great Nebulas. It didn't feel real that I'd already reached a position where I could hear that said about us.

The twelve nebulas that dominated <Star Stream>: three strong (强), four middle (中), and five weak (弱). <Olympus>, which had fluctuated between the top three and the middle four, had just suffered a heavy blow. Someone was bound to try to fill the gap.
“A lot of stars are getting ahead of themselves.”
[That's how the gossipmongers always are.]
“And you, ‘Mass Production Maker’, would like to take the opportunity to sign a contract with our nebula.”
[Precisely.]
There wasn't a trace of hesitation in his answer.
[I'm thinking of having your nebula advertise my new product. What do you say?]
“I'd be happy to. I'll ask the others in the nebula, too.”
[Excellent. As for the incarnations I'd personally like to appear······.]

Listening to ‘Mass Production Maker’, I watched the scenery pass beyond the [Ferrarghini]'s window. Countless seasons of stories flowed through that passing landscape. From spring to summer, then autumn.
Yes. Before I knew it······.
“······It's fast.”
The words slipped out as I gripped the bottle of Star Relic Liquid against my chest.
I'd made it this far faster than in any round of the original novel. But that speed was only relative. I didn't know whether it was ‘fast enough’.
‘Mass Production Maker’ laughed heartily as he spoke.
[This new model is rather fast. You'll see if you drive it yourself, but the handling is absolutely······.]
“It's taking an awfully long time for the speed we're doing. You're not taking a detour just to discuss the contract, are you?”
[Ahem. What are you talking about? This is the fastest route. Look, we're already at the last junction.]
As ‘Mass Production Maker’ said, three portals were shining white across the pitch-black dimensional road. Without being asked, ‘Mass Production Maker’ added an explanation.
[One leads to Earth. Another leads to the ‘context of my constellation’.]
“What about the last one?”
[A ‘road that looks like a road’.]
Mass Production Maker said with a meaningful smile.
A portal much darker than the others, giving off a damp, gloomy air.
[Do you know what's at the end of it?]
Of course, I didn't.
Not even ‘Ways of Survival’ described every portal along the dimensional roads. In other words, that ‘portal’ would be a road that didn't exist in ‘Ways of Survival’.
“What's there?”
[Nothing. It's simply a dead end.]
An answer delivered as though it were perfectly obvious.
Before I could reply, ‘Mass Production Maker’ continued.
[Some roads end like that. You walk them because they look different, or because you think no one has taken them before. But often, they weren't even roads to begin with.]
The [Ferrarghini] accelerated past the gloomy portal. The glowing navigation display showed the route to Earth.
On the screen, the portal we'd just passed was marked ‘No Road’.
[Such roads usually break off in some uncertain place. And those who chose to walk them must go on living, believing that was the end.]
“······What are you trying to tell me?”
[Please choose your road carefully.]
‘Mass Production Maker’, who had already put out his cigar, spoke with his usual gentlemanly smile.
[Sometimes, what looked like a road may never have been a road at all.]
The next moment, the dimensional scenery changed. I caught a glimpse of a blue planet, and suddenly I had landed on the ground.
‘Mass Production Maker’ spoke.
[We're here. Fortunately, it seems we arrived at the right place this time.]
The place I headed for as soon as I reached Seoul was, needless to say, the [Factory]. More specifically, the ward where the patients were staying.
The moment I stepped inside, a voice almost like a [True Voice] rang out.
[You've come.]
It sounded like a [True Voice], but it wasn't one. A voice bearing a transcendent's dignity.
Baekchung's magic power, crackling blue in the air.
······It seemed all masters wanted their disciples to see them in the same light, after all.
“Your unworthy disciple greets you.”
[We have no time. I'll accept your greeting later. Go.]
Kyrgios was wrapped in bandages, perhaps from the ‘Returnee War’.
“What about the Blood Demon and the Heavenly Demon······?”
[I killed them. Stop talking and go.]

I inwardly marveled at that calm declaration. He had faced the Blood Demon and the Heavenly Demon alone, opponents even the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint of a previous life couldn't defeat, and survived. I could barely grasp how much stronger my master had grown in this round.
Aileen spotted me from a distance and came running. The only Story Expert guarding the [Factory]. Without her, two or three of our companions would already have died.
I pulled the Star Relic Liquid from my coat and waved it as I shouted:
“I brought Star Relic Liquid!”
“There's something I didn't get a chance to tell you······.”
“I know the situation.”
Two hospital rooms glowed red in the distance.
One was Yoo Sangah's. The other······.
“How is my mother?”
“Her symptoms are almost the same as Yoo Sangah-ssi's.”
“How severe?”
“If anything, they're worse. Certainly no less······.”
I knew my mother had been pushing herself too hard.

Stigmas that foresaw the ‘great future’ put a heavy burden on their users. That burden would have been far worse for Yoo Sangah, whose contract with an entire nebula was ambiguous, and my mother, whose sponsor had lost almost all her power.
Taking the liquid from me, Aileen spoke in a grim voice.
“I don't think this will be enough.”
“That's why I brought two bottles. Different kinds, too.”
I hadn't brought just one kind. Besides the [Soma] Surya had promised, I had the [Nectar] I'd taken from Dionysus.
For a moment, Aileen's face brightened as she took the two bottles.
“······Medical team!”

The physicians who ran over at her signal headed for the two rooms all at once. Someone brushed against me on the way past, sending a fierce ache through the side Poseidon had struck. My vision blurred for a moment, then cleared.
······Maybe I needed treatment, too.
Then again, it would have been stranger to be fine after taking a Myth-grade constellation's attack.

I forced myself to steady my breathing to hide the pain. Perhaps because my consciousness was unstable, the doors the physicians entered looked just like the portals ‘Mass Production Maker’ had shown me.
[Are you all right?]
Kyrgios flew over to ask me. I answered that I was fine. More precisely, I seemed to have answered, and also to have lost consciousness for a moment.
When I came to, I was lying on a chair in the ward.
Aileen stood before me.
Enduring the pain, I got up.
“······How are they?”
I forced my clouding consciousness into focus as I asked.
But there was something wrong with Aileen's expression.
“······It's not enough.”
“Not enough? What isn't?”
“Their conditions worsened much faster than we expected. I think we'd need both bottles of Star Relic Liquid just to treat one of them.”
I couldn't understand her. In that moment, Aileen's words sounded like a distant alien language. Like an Outer God's gibberish.
“What······does that mean?”
“Demon King of Salvation-nim.”
It had been a long time since Aileen addressed me by my modifier. She only called me that when she needed an order.
The two rooms stood wide open, like portals waiting for me.
“We can save only one person.”
All kinds of thoughts flashed through my head.
[‘Fourth Wall’ shakes violently.]
There were two doors. It was as though someone were whispering to me.
Go in, if you want.
But if you choose one, you must abandon the other.
······There was no way I could.
“Demon King of Salvation-nim.”
“If you delay any longer, we won't be able to save either of them.”
Aileen's voice sounded unreal.
“Please give me a moment.”
As my vision swam, I could see the ward's corridor running between the two rooms.
The words of ‘Mass Production Maker’ crossed my mind.
―Nothing. It's simply a dead end.
The corridor's end was too dark to see, but everyone knew there was nothing there.
A corridor designed to have nothing at its end.
「Kim Dokja thought: That can't be right.」
Stay calm. There is a way.
I'd come all this way, and now I had to choose one of them?
Who was I supposed to save, and who was I supposed to kill?
I couldn't do that.
[‘Fourth Wall’ looks at you.]
「B u t you've cho sen be fore.」
The ‘first scenario’ flashed through my head. The swaying subway. People lying dead. People I might have been able to save—all of them.
「S o you can cho ose a gain this time.」
······This isn't like then.
「W hat's dif fer ent?」
Instead of answering [Fourth Wall], I asked Aileen:
“How much time do we have?”
“About twenty minutes······Lee Sookyung-ssi is in a slightly more critical condition. If more time passes, even that will no longer be······.”
Twenty minutes.
Not long, but enough to try a few things.
It was too early to give up.
“If we had more Star Relic Liquid, could we save them both?”
“······There might be a chance.”
I immediately took out [Old to New Toad].
With a croak, the toad spoke.
―G ive me the old, I'll give you the new.
I pointed to the half-full bottle of [Nectar] and asked:
“Could you exchange this for a ‘new’ one, too?”
But [Old to New Toad] shook its head.
―T hat is nei ther old nor new.
“I drank half of this. That makes it old. I'll give you another item, so if you could refill this bottle to make it new again······.”
―S oph is try······That isn't some thing I can grant.
As expected, it seemed tricks like this wouldn't work on an item like Star Relic Liquid. I'd thought it might work.
―I'm ti red. Don't ca ll me.
Perhaps swallowing the ‘Giant Soldier’ and making it new earlier had exhausted it. With those words, [Old to New Toad] fell fast asleep.
I put it away and decided to try a second method.
If I couldn't duplicate it, I'd have to get more.
[Demon King ‘Demon King of Salvation’······.]
Tzzzzzt!
[Indirect message use has been canceled.]
[Indirect messages are currently disabled due to maintenance and repairs on a particular scenario.]
[The scenario under maintenance is ‘Scenario 60’.]
An unforeseen coincidence. I hadn't imagined the fierce fighting in Scenario 60 would have repercussions all the way here······.
But I needed help from other constellations to get more Star Relic Liquid.
“Jang Hayoung!”
At my shout, Aileen looked in a certain direction.
As luck would have it, Jang Hayoung was hospitalized in Yoo Sangah's room. A chill crept over the back of my neck as I stood on the threshold beneath the emergency light.
“You can't just come in!”
Someone shouted at me.
Story fragments drifted through the air from where Yoo Sangah lay.
I forced myself to look away and pushed past the physicians to find Jang Hayoung.
Jang Hayoung lay asleep in the room's right-hand corner.
“Jang Hayoung! Wake up! Hurry!”
“Wait! That patient is in critical condition, too!”
The physicians rushed over to pull me back.
Looking closer, I saw that Jang Hayoung was wrapped in bandages and receiving a large number of Story Packs. The ‘Returnee War’ had left Hayoung badly injured, too.
But I desperately needed Jang Hayoung's skill.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ looks at you.]
[‘Fourth Wall’ faces ‘Unidentifiable Wall’.]
Sparks flickered before me, and I felt the wall's impersonal gaze.
An icy indifference without the slightest desire to cooperate.
······So that's how you want to play it?
I opened [Bookmark].
In the end, ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ was a ‘skill,’ too.
My understanding of ‘Jang Hayoung’ was still low, so I'd need a little luck······.
I began searching the [Bookmark] list for the name ‘Jang Hayoung’.
Perhaps sensing something unpleasant in my actions, ‘Unidentifiable Wall’ spoke in warning.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says: ‘You are not my master. Don't do anything useless.’]
“I need your help.”
I spoke honestly. Every minute, every second, counted.
“If you don't help me, I'll have to wake your master.”
For a while, the wall didn't answer. Silence, as though it were thinking something over.
After a moment, a message came from the other side.
[‘Unidentifiable Wall’ says: ‘······I'll help.’]
At those words, a small partitioned space formed around me. It reminded me of my office long ago, when I was an intern at Mino Soft.

Reincarnation Island.

The constellation’s incarnation body, collapsing in a daze as though it hadn’t even realized what had happened to it.

Constellations who had reigned from the thrones of the <Star Stream>, resplendent in their power and prestige, died because they couldn’t overcome mere infectious diseases or orcs.

Constellations dying to the low-grade monsters they had always dismissed······.

Croak.
